description: verify_import skips the graph-topology assertion whenever either side's Cozo DB is absent. If v1 has a graph and the v2 graph namespace was never written (import interrupted after vectors/KV, or deleted), the result is 'verified' with no graph check.
evidence: `v1_graph = _v1_graph(...)`; `v2_graph = _v2_graph(...)`; `if v1_graph is not None and v2_graph is not None:` (455-457). _v2_graph returns None when `<store_root>/<workspace>/chunk_entity_relation/graph.cozo` does not exist (382-385). The 'refused' precondition only checks that the workspace directory exists (409). Same pattern for chunk text: _v1_text_chunks returns {} when v1 KV file is missing (262-266), so v2-only chunks are never flagged.
gui_impact: A re-import or verify panel would show a green 'verified' for a LightRAG store whose graph is missing; the graph browser would then show an empty graph under a verified badge.

description: When v1's aquery_data returns a non-success status, the driver silently sets data={} and returns empty chunk/entity/relation id lists with exit 0, and still runs aquery for an answer. The module docstring says a v1-side query failure exits 1 and is never an empty success.
evidence: Line 127: `data = data_response.get("data") or {} if data_response.get("status") == "success" else {}` (parses as `(...) if status == 'success' else {}`). Docstring 38-40: 'A malformed job, a v1-side query failure, or any other exception prints a traceback to stderr and exits 1 ... never as an empty success.' v1_arm.py:171-183 then builds a V1ArmResult with empty id tuples.
gui_impact: A comparison view would show the v1 arm as having retrieved nothing (recall 0) instead of a refusal, misattributing a v1 failure to retrieval quality.

description: hl_keywords_used/ll_keywords_used fall back to the caller's own input when v1's metadata.keywords is missing or empty, so the field is not guaranteed to be v1's echo. The docstring says these are read back from v1's response, 'not a value this script merely reflects on its own behalf'.
evidence: `hl_keywords_used = [str(k) for k in (used_keywords.get("high_level") or hl_keywords)]` (140) and same for low_level (141). Docstring 31-36 claims the echo is the mechanism that proves pinned keywords reached v1.
gui_impact: A keyword-provenance display for the v1 arm can show pinned keywords as 'used by v1' when v1 reported nothing.

description: With hl_keywords and ll_keywords both empty (the v1_arm CLI default, v1_arm.py:198-199) and mode local/global/hybrid/mix, v1 extracts keywords through the LLM once in aquery_data and again in aquery (LLM cache off), so the comments at v1_driver_script.py:71 and 143-144 are false. naive and bypass are unaffected. The discarded keyword_extraction flag has no effect because v1 never sets it.
evidence: `del keyword_extraction  # unused — this script never lets v1 extract its own keywords` (71); `QueryParam(mode=mode, hl_keywords=hl_keywords, ll_keywords=ll_keywords)` with possibly empty lists (121); v1_arm.py:198-199 `--hl-keyword`/`--ll-keyword` default `[]`.
gui_impact: A v1-arm run without pinned keywords spends an extra unaccounted LLM call and its retrieval is not comparable to a pinned decomposed run.

description: Retrieved ids and the prose answer come from two separate v1 query executions (aquery_data then aquery). With LLM cache disabled (v1_arm.py:149), the answer's retrieval is not guaranteed to be the retrieval whose ids are reported.
evidence: `data_response = await rag.aquery_data(query.strip(), param)` (126); `answer = await rag.aquery(query.strip(), param)` (145); `env.setdefault("ENABLE_LLM_CACHE", "false")` (v1_arm.py:149).
gui_impact: An evidence view pairing v1's answer with v1's chunk ids may pair an answer with ids it was not generated from.

description: The CLI exits 0 for a cyclic wiring (zero rows) and for a partial run. A partial run leaves undispatched nodes with no touches, which are reported as 'no-touch' rather than as unreached, and the 'partial' flag returned by run_audit is never printed or checked.
evidence: Cycle: `return {"cycle": ..., "rows": [], "violations": [], "partial": False}` (207); main only checks `violations` (254-258) and never reads result['partial'] or result['cycle']. audit_run marks any declared-but-untouched node 'no-touch' (132-133) regardless of whether it ran.
gui_impact: An audit table would show budget-halted or failed nodes as legitimate 'no-touch' and a cyclic wiring as a clean 0-node pass.

description: main catches only MissingParityEnvError; a missing key in the env file raises MissingParityEnvKeyError from run_arm._build_clients and escapes as a traceback instead of a one-line exit 1. build_hipporag_index.main catches both (build_hipporag_index.py:339-343).
evidence: `except _run_arm.MissingParityEnvError as exc:` (243); run_arm.py:170 `raise MissingParityEnvKeyError(missing)`; MissingParityEnvKeyError subclasses RuntimeError directly (run_arm.py:74), not MissingParityEnvError.
gui_impact: none directly (CLI); a wrapped audit endpoint copying this handler would map a config error to 500.

description: The audit can only run LightRAG arms: it resolves through resolve_arm (LightRAG patch files only) and builds stores without the resolved wiring, so HippoRAG wirings and their store_namespaces are not auditable.
evidence: `resolved = resolve_arm(arm_name)` (173); `_run_arm._build_stores(resolved_store_root, resolved_workspace)` with no `resolved` argument (180), so kv/graph fall back to text_chunks/chunk_entity_relation (run_arm.py:207-209); `--arm` choices are the five LightRAG arms (237), matching databasise/wirings/lightrag/arm-*.json-patch.json.
gui_impact: A per-node effects audit panel cannot cover the HippoRAG modality without new code.

description: The module docstring (build_hipporag_index.py:32-37) says the build was never invoked, but CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md:140-149 and 197-212 record real invocations on 2026-09-10, the second of which exited 0. hipporag-chunks/-entities/-facts/-graph/-text-chunks exist under v1/.parity_v2_store/shared-4fab18fef508b7bc3dda1cc2d8f12e36/ with files dated 2026-09-10. The evidence document's own lines 27-31 are also stale.
evidence: build_hipporag_index.py:32-37; databasise/evidence/CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md:144-149 and 210 ('uv run python -m databasise.parity.build_hipporag_index was invoked first against live ...'); `ls v1/.parity_v2_store/*/` lists hipporag-chunks, hipporag-entities, hipporag-facts, hipporag-graph, hipporag-text-chunks.
gui_impact: none (documentation only); but anyone reading the docstring would assume no HippoRAG data exists to browse.

description: The HippoRAG build refuses unless the LightRAG import directory exists at store_root/workspace, although nothing in the HippoRAG wiring reads LightRAG namespaces; it only uses that directory as the shared workspace. Separately, the post-build check verifies entity and fact vector counts but not the hipporag-chunks count it also computes.
evidence: `if not lightrag_dir.exists(): raise MissingParityLightRAGIndexError(lightrag_dir)` (176-178); failures list (291-303) has no check on chunk_vector_count (computed at 284).
gui_impact: A 'build HippoRAG index' action would fail on a store root that has no LightRAG import, and could report success with an empty chunk namespace.

description: The 'refused' result (no v2 store at all) is labelled with assertion='chunk-text', which is not the failed check; the Violation type has no precondition value.
evidence: `Violation(assertion="chunk-text", detail=f"no imported v2 store found at ...")` (413-418); Violation.assertion Literal is limited to chunk-text/vector-tolerance/graph-topology (108).
gui_impact: A verify panel grouping violations by assertion would show a missing store as a chunk-text failure.

description: The importer CLI (import_index.py:498-511) hard-codes v1/.parity_working_dir and the derived parity workspace, and no CLI flag or REST/MCP route imports v1/.corpus_working_dir. The function import_v1_index(v1_working_dir, store_root, workspace) (231-254) accepts any v1 working directory, and v1/.corpus_working_dir has a compatible layout, so a re-import of engine-ingested LightRAG documents needs only a new caller, not a new importer.
evidence: DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = v1/.parity_working_dir (84); main() calls `import_v1_index(DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR, DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT)` (510); foreign/v1_corpus_adapter.py:31 `DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = _REPO_ROOT / "v1" / ".corpus_working_dir"`. Both directories exist on disk.
gui_impact: A 're-import' button wired to this importer would re-import the fixed 20-document parity corpus, not what the operator ingested through /corpus.

description: The imported LightRAG data lives under a derived workspace hash (derive_namespace over fixed recipe strings and the corpus hash), and the engine reads only the store_root/workspace passed to its constructor. The engine sees the parity import only if it is launched with store_root=v1/.parity_v2_store and workspace equal to that hash (currently shared-4fab18fef508b7bc3dda1cc2d8f12e36 per CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md:31). Nothing exposes or documents that value to a launcher.
evidence: _import_workspace (119-134); Databasise.__init__ stores caller-supplied store_root/workspace (engine.py:547-553); no seam/, mcp/ or foreign/ module imports databasise.parity (grep of import statements returns nothing).
gui_impact: The console launcher must be given this exact workspace string to show any LightRAG graph/vector data; otherwise LightRAG browse and evidence views are empty.

description: A missing v1/.env.parity is not refused by name: v1_arm.py:109-110 returns {} by design (IN-01, 104-108). The driver then raises KeyError, wrapped as V1ArmSubprocessError, or, if v1/.env exists, v1's import-time load_dotenv('.env') with cwd=v1 (lightrag.py:159, base.py:36, llm/openai.py:71) supplies a different configuration and the run proceeds silently.
evidence: `if not path.exists(): return {}` (109-110); driver reads `os.environ["LLM_MODEL"]`, `os.environ["EMBEDDING_DIM"]`, `os.environ["LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE"]` etc. without defaults.
gui_impact: A v1-arm run from a console would show a raw subprocess traceback instead of a named configuration error.

description: parse_wiring assumes doc is a dict and doc['nodes'] is a dict. nodes=None or a list, or a non-dict doc, raises AttributeError instead of accumulating a violation, contradicting the module docstring (parse.py:5-7: 'parse_wiring never raises for an ordinary defect'). For nodes=None the CODE_EMPTY_WIRING violation is appended and then the loop crashes.
evidence: Reproduced with databasise/.venv/bin/python: parse_wiring({'nodes': None}, default_registry()) -> AttributeError 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'items'; {'nodes': [1]} -> AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'items'; doc=[] -> AttributeError 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. Line 143 `raw_nodes: dict[str, Any] = doc.get("nodes", {})`, line 155 `for node_id, raw in raw_nodes.items()`.
gui_impact: Low today because wiring documents come only from shipped JSON files (wirings/resolve.py), not request bodies. If a future GET /wirings/validation or wiring-upload route feeds operator-supplied documents, a malformed document gives a 500 instead of a violation list.

description: Two functions named derive_execution_mode with different mappings. The depth.py version is unused in production (only tests/parts/test_reference_parts.py:19 imports it) and its module docstring (depth.py:1, 27-33) still claims its _REQUIRES_CONTAINMENT set is 'refused by name at the runner (D-08)'. The runner uses execution_mode.py's version (runner/scheduler.py:137-139, 422).
evidence: Probe output: ['calls_llm'],'stage' -> depth: subprocess, execution_mode: in-process; [],'fixpoint' -> subprocess vs long-lived-service; ['self_storage'],'stage' -> in-process vs confined-unit; ['fs'],'stage' -> subprocess vs confined-unit. parts_core/fixpoint_body.py:8 still cites validator.depth.derive_execution_mode; test_reference_parts.py:93 asserts the dead version returns 'subprocess' for the fixpoint part while the runner derives 'long-lived-service' for it.
gui_impact: A GUI or doc that shows execution_mode must use execution_mode.py; anyone reading depth.py or fixpoint_body.py gets the wrong placement. Test test_reference_parts.py asserts a placement the runner never uses.

description: CONTRACT.md:238 says 'only pure, non-iterative nodes MAY be hosted in-process'. The live derivation returns 'in-process' for nodes declaring calls_llm, calls_embedding, calls_rerank and the writes_* store effects, because only net/fs/self_storage/mutates_store, opaque and fixpoint leave in-process. A node calling an LLM API is not pure. The superseded depth.py version (depth.py:34-36) did route calls_llm/calls_rerank/calls_embedding out of in-process.
evidence: derive_execution_mode(['calls_llm'], 'stage') == 'in-process' (probe). _NOT_IN_PROCESS_EFFECTS = {'net','fs','self_storage','mutates_store'} (execution_mode.py:41-43). tests/parts_core/hipporag/test_thirteen_positions.py:114-119 asserts in-process for all thirteen HippoRAG positions, which include LLM-calling parts. Whether 'pure' admits client calls through machine-owned clients is a contract interpretation; the module docstring (execution_mode.py:7-10) records the mapping as a discretionary choice.
gui_impact: A placement badge in the console would show LLM-calling nodes as in-process. Operators judging containment would read that as pure.

description: The stale Phase-1 refusal text (execution_mode.py:91-94) is not limited to logs: for ingest/delete it reaches the REST refusal body through ForeignEngineRefusalError.message and .cause (engine.py:385-387, refusals.py:502, rest.py:220-230). On the query path only the stop_reason summary 'execution_mode=<mode> not hosted (D-08)' appears (scheduler.py:594-596).
evidence: execution_mode.py:51-53 'Phase 1 implements in-process hosting only (D-08); subprocess/confined-unit/long-lived-service are refused by name'; execution_mode.py:85-87 returns for subprocess with ceiling > 0.
gui_impact: The refusal text flows into stop_reason (scheduler.py:595) only as 'execution_mode=<mode> not hosted (D-08)'; the stale Phase-1 text appears in exception chains/logs an operator might read.

description: WiringValidationError is never raised (its own docstring says so). The runner raises its own WiringRefusedError (runner/scheduler.py:179-187) instead.
evidence: grep for WiringValidationError outside databasise/validator returns no hits.
gui_impact: None directly; a client mapping refusal names from source would find a class that never occurs.

description: ParsedWiring docstring claims 'every collection here is a read-only view ... never a plain mutable dict or list'. report is a non-frozen ValidationReport whose violations/cycles are plain lists, and parse_wiring itself mutates report.violations after building the frozen snapshot (line 253). WiringNode values are also mutable pydantic models (parts/schema.py:156 sets only extra='forbid', not frozen).
evidence: errors.py:49 `@dataclass` (not frozen), `violations: list[Violation]`; parse.py:253 `report.violations.extend(blast_radius_violations(parsed, depth_map))`.
gui_impact: None for the GUI; relevant to CONTRACT §11 'no mid-run reads of mutable decision state' claims.

description: A node with a self-loop that is also part of a larger SCC is reported twice in report.cycles: once in the multi-member SCC and once as a one-member self-loop.
evidence: Probe: nodes a(deps [a,b]) and b(deps [a]) -> report.cycles == [['a','b'], ['a']].
gui_impact: A cycle list in a validation view would show duplicate/overlapping entries; the runner's {'cycle': ...} payload (scheduler.py:529) carries the same duplication.

description: Violation.pointer is documented as an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, but node ids are interpolated without escaping '~' to '~0' and '/' to '~1'. Node ids are not constrained to exclude these characters.
evidence: Probe: node id 'x/y' with unknown component -> pointer '/nodes/x/y/component', which RFC 6901 resolves to nodes -> x -> y -> component.
gui_impact: A GUI that highlights the offending JSON location by resolving the pointer would point at the wrong (or a non-existent) element.

description: WiringNode.kind is not validated against the resolved Part.kind. The runner ignores it (placement uses part.kind, scheduler.py:422), but Databasise.ingest uses the wiring's declared kind to gate raw uploads (engine.py:690), so a mismatched declared kind changes ingest behaviour: an 'opaque' declaration on a non-opaque part would admit a raw upload, and a non-'opaque' declaration on an opaque part would refuse one.
evidence: Probe: node with component 'parts-core/passthrough@1.0.0' (Part.kind 'passthrough') declared kind 'fixpoint' -> report.ok True.
gui_impact: A DAG view that renders the wiring's kind field can show a node kind the machine does not use.

description: Top-level wiring fields (provides, evidence_position, store_namespaces, consumes_query, harnesses) are not validated. A provides entry naming a non-existent node passes validation and default eligibility (selectors.py:199-200); at run time the query path silently returns an empty answer with depth_label 'stage' (engine.py:502-505, 1035-1037), and ingest/delete refuse with ForeignEngineRefusalError (engine.py:388-393).
evidence: parse.py:143 reads only doc.get('nodes'); selectors.py:199-200 `provides = resolved.get('provides') or []; return all(depths.get(node_id) != 'opaque' ...)`.
gui_impact: A wiring validation report would not flag a broken provides/evidence_position reference; such defects surface later as engine 500s (for example engine.py:502-507).

description: Docstring justifies reading artifact_scope via getattr because the field 'may not have landed yet' in parts/schema.py. Part now declares artifact_scope: ArtifactScope | None = None (parts/schema.py:140), so the getattr fallback and its rationale are stale.
evidence: parts/schema.py:140 `artifact_scope: ArtifactScope | None = None`.
gui_impact: None.

description: CODE_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT message is str(UnknownPartError); UnknownPartError subclasses KeyError (parts/registry.py:24), so the message is wrapped in an extra pair of quotes and embeds the full list of all ~35 registered part names.
evidence: Probe message: '"unknown part \'nope\'; registered parts: [...35 names...]"' (leading/trailing double quote from KeyError.__str__).
gui_impact: Validation panel text is noisy and quoted; GUI should render code + pointer and truncate message.

description: A non-ok ValidationReport is raised as WiringRefusedError, a plain ValueError rather than a SeamRefusalError, so REST returns an unstructured 500 and the structured Violation list (code/pointer/message) is flattened into the exception string. Cycle reports are returned as data by run_wiring but only the query path converts them to an error (engine.py:1002-1006, RuntimeError); the ingest (engine.py:732) and delete (engine.py:824) paths do not check for the 'cycle' key.
evidence: scheduler.py:179 `class WiringRefusedError(ValueError)`; rest.py:250 registers a handler only for SeamRefusalError; grep for '"cycle"' in seam/ finds only engine.py:1002.
gui_impact: The GUI cannot show which violation refused a run; it receives a 500. A cyclic ingest/delete wiring would fail on a missing 'results' key instead of a named error.

description: compare_arm_on_query never checks the decomposed run's partial/degraded/cycle state before computing diffs and returning status="completed". A budget halt, a failed node, or a cycle yields empty or truncated id lists, which are diffed against v1 and reported as a completed comparison showing large disagreement.
evidence: _run_decomposed_arm returns {"cycle":..., "resolved":...} with no "results" key on a cycle (369-370); _extract_decomposed_ids(decomposed.get("results", {})) then yields [] (590-592); the record is built with status="completed" (629-647) without reading run_record["partial"]/["degraded"]. The module docstring (9-13) states that a confounded comparison returning a normal-looking verdict is worse than a refusal, and run_cross_modality.py:338-348 refuses exactly this case.
gui_impact: A parity view built from these JSON files would show partial runs as real retrieval disagreement. The GUI must read decomposed_run_record.partial/degraded itself and flag such rows.

description: The index-identity pre-flight checks a different v1 working directory than the v1 arm runs against when v1_working_dir is overridden. verify_fn is called without v1_working_dir, so it verifies DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR, while run_v1_arm uses the override.
evidence: verify_kwargs only receives store_root and workspace (530-534); verify_import's signature takes v1_working_dir=DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR (import_index.py:397-401); run_v1_arm gets working_dir=v1_working_dir or DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR (603).
gui_impact: None today (CLI never passes v1_working_dir), but any GUI or route that exposes a v1 working dir parameter would get a verified pre-flight for the wrong index.

description: Pre-flight does not check that the LightRAG index is non-empty; it only checks that the workspace directory exists. The docstrings (11-12, 221-222) say both arms' indexes are checked present and non-empty at their own declared namespaces. The workspace directory is shared by both arms, so a built HippoRAG index alone satisfies the LightRAG check.
evidence: LightRAG check: `lightrag_index_dir = Path(store_root) / workspace; if not lightrag_index_dir.exists()` (230-235). Only HippoRAG gets _vector_namespace_non_empty(..., "hipporag-chunks") (236). build_hipporag_index writes into the same store_root/workspace (build_hipporag_index.py:201-202, 220).
gui_impact: A preflight panel derived from this logic would report LightRAG ready when its chunks namespace is empty.

description: Preflight is not read-only: it mkdirs every LightRAG and HippoRAG kv/graph/vector namespace directory and creates sqlite/Cozo files in the live store, and never calls finalize(). Under CPython the handles are released when _resolved_store_dirs returns, so the following engine.compare is not blocked (verified). A GUI readiness check run while another holder has the same Cozo graph path open would fail with a RocksDB lock error.
evidence: kv.py:51-52, graph.py:104-107 and vector.py:115-116 mkdir/open in __init__; graph.py:376-378 is the only close path (finalize); preflight never calls it (242-247). pycozo Client defines close but no __del__ (checked via dir(pycozo.client.Client)). Not reproduced: a reopen test was not permitted in this session, so the lock risk is PLAUSIBLE, the mkdir side effect is CONFIRMED by code.
gui_impact: A 'check readiness' button that reuses this preflight would create empty namespace directories and Cozo files in the live store and could contend for the RocksDB lock with a running query.

description: The arms actually run are chosen by capability selectors, while the recipe hashes recorded in preflight come from resolve_arm("naive") and load_wiring("hipporag"). Nothing checks that the selectors resolve to those two wirings. Today [reads_graph, reads_kv] resolves to hipporag only because it has 13 nodes versus 15 for local/global (smallest-wiring tie-break, selectors.py:149-164). If the HippoRAG wiring grows past 15 nodes, the second arm silently becomes LightRAG local, the run is LightRAG vs LightRAG, and the record still reports a HippoRAG recipe hash.
evidence: Measured: naive 7 nodes, local 15, global 15, hybrid 17, hipporag 13; _resolve_capability([reads_graph, reads_kv]) returned wiring_id hipporag-base, _resolve_capability([reads_vector]) returned lightrag-base with 7 nodes (naive). preflight hashes: 256-258.
gui_impact: A GUI that compares modalities by capability selector has the same problem: the selector key (e.g. 'reads_graph+reads_kv') does not identify which wiring ran, and no route reports the resolved wiring per arm.

description: The partial/degraded refusal is raised only after every query has run, and the raise discards all collected per-query records. Tokens are spent on all queries, and no record of which query/arm degraded is written.
evidence: any_degraded is set inside the loop (338-339) and checked after it (344-348); main catches DegradedCrossModalityRunError and returns 1 without writing JSON (395-403).
gui_impact: If a GUI drives this flow, a degraded arm leaves the operator with no per-query detail; the GUI would need to call /compare per query itself to see which arm degraded.

description: Confirmed for MissingParityEnvKeyError/UnparseableProviderRoutingError in run_arm.main and run_comparison._run_cli, and for UnparseableProviderRoutingError plus seam refusals in run_cross_modality.main. SingleRunBandError is unreachable from the run_comparison CLI (default keyword_variance_runs=5, not exposed). Only programmatic callers of compare_arm_on_query can trigger it.
evidence: run_arm.py:358 `except MissingParityEnvError`; run_comparison.py:700 `except (MissingParityEnvError, MissingV1InterpreterError, V1ArmSubprocessError)`; run_cross_modality.py:395-401 list omits UnparseableProviderRoutingError (defined run_arm.py:132). SingleRunBandError is raised by compute_keyword_variance_band (168-172) at 578 after the pinning call already spent tokens.
gui_impact: Low directly; a GUI wrapper around these functions must catch these exception types itself.

description: keyword_variance_runs is not validated before tokens are spent. Values 0 or 1 make compute_keyword_variance_band raise SingleRunBandError only after the pinning call and the 0-1 band calls have run. run_count is reported as 0 for arms without a keywords node even though one decomposed and one v1 run happened, and also 0 for inconclusive records (496), so the field does not distinguish 'no runs' from 'no keyword runs'.
evidence: pin call 569, band list 574-577, band computed 578; run_count expression 637; inconclusive run_count=0 at 496.
gui_impact: A parity table showing run_count would display 0 for completed naive/bypass comparisons.

description: Internal consistency drift: _run_decomposed_arm (run_comparison.py:355) omits the resolved wiring when building stores, which the run_arm.py:201-205 docstring says must not happen. There is no behavioural difference today and no CONTRACT.md violation.
evidence: run_comparison.py:355 `stores = _build_stores(store_root, workspace)`; run_arm.py:294 `_build_stores(resolved_store_root, resolved_workspace, resolved)`.
gui_impact: None today.

description: Module docstring says the harness has not been invoked for real and points to CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md as BLOCKED. A real result file exists and git history records the completed run.
evidence: databasise/parity/.comparison_results/cross_modality.json (Sep 10) has 2 queries, arms reads_vector (10 items) and reads_graph+reads_kv (20 items), partial/degraded false; commit 650d074 'docs(06-15): record the completed real cross-modality run and discharge MODAL-05'.
gui_impact: None; affects anyone using the docstring to decide whether cross-modality results exist.

description: When a caller overrides queries, the record still stamps corpus_hash from the default snapshot, so a record over a custom query list claims the default corpus identity.
evidence: snapshot = load_snapshot() always (301); queries override used at 319; corpus_hash=snapshot.corpus_hash (351).
gui_impact: If the GUI passes its own query list through this function, the recorded corpus_hash is not tied to those queries.

description: main re-imports json inside the function although it is imported at module level; --arm choices are hard-coded to the five LightRAG arms, so this driver cannot run the hipporag wiring (resolve_arm is LightRAG-only).
evidence: run_arm.py:29 `import json` and 349 `import json`; 352 choices list; run_arm uses resolve_arm (287).
gui_impact: None directly; confirms no per-modality single-arm driver exists outside the seam for HippoRAG.

description: Guards are evaluated against `results` at the moment the guarded node completes, and `evaluating_node` is never validated to exist or to have already run. If evaluating_node is a downstream node, a same-batch sibling sorted after the guarded node, or a misspelt id, `runtime_values.get(...)` returns None and the guard is reported as fired whenever value_when_not_fired is not None.
evidence: scheduler.py:639 assigns results[node_id] inside the sorted per-batch loop, then 651 calls evaluate_guards(guards_by_node[node_id], results); guards.py:83 `runtime_values.get(guard.evaluating_node) != guard.value_when_not_fired`; _validated_guards (scheduler.py:386-387) checks only granularity via declare_guard. The one shipped guard avoids this only because evaluating_node equals the guarded node itself (wirings/hipporag/base.json:72-73).
gui_impact: guards_fired in the node table can show a false positive; a compare could be refused under CONTRACT §5's tenth condition on a guard that did not fire.

description: evaluate_guards compares the evaluating node's entire output object to a scalar sentinel. Any ordinary dict output always differs from false/null, so a guard always fires unless the part returns a dict subclass that overrides __eq__/__ne__. The only working guard relies on exactly that workaround.
evidence: guards.py:83 compares the whole value; parts_core/hipporag/fact_filter.py:62-85 defines `_GuardAwareResult(dict)` with custom __eq__/__ne__ solely so `!=` against `false` reads `guard_fired`.
gui_impact: Any new part with a guard will report guards_fired on every run; operator cannot trust the column outside HippoRAG fact-filter.

description: arm-local declares ll_keywords_empty_fallthrough and arm-global declares hl_keywords_empty_fallthrough, both in a top-level patch 'guards' array that resolve.py:108 ignores. Neither guard reaches config.guards or is evaluated, and the declared shape (guard_name, no granularity) would raise TypeError in declare_guard(**entry).
evidence: resolve.py:108 `operations = patch_doc["operations"]`; no Python reads the patch `guards` key (grep for `guards` under wirings/, seam/, validator/, parity/ outside runner returns nothing). If moved into config.guards as written, declare_guard(**entry) would raise TypeError on `guard_name`.
gui_impact: guards_fired is always [] for local/global arms even when the documented fallthrough happens; compare panels cannot show guard divergence for LightRAG arms.

description: Docstring says a malformed guard names the offending node via GuardDeclarationError's fields; GuardDeclarationError carries only guard_name and granularity, not node_id. A guard entry with a missing/extra key or a non-dict entry raises a bare TypeError from `declare_guard(**entry)`, not GuardDeclarationError (the WR-04 lesson the sibling validators follow).
evidence: scheduler.py:383-384 claim; guards.py:36-42 has no node_id; scheduler.py:387 `declare_guard(**entry)`.
gui_impact: A bad guard declaration surfaces as an unattributed 500 with no node id.

description: Pre-flight scheduler errors are not SeamRefusalError and would surface as an unstructured 500. With shipped wirings and the engine's injected allowance, only WiringRefusedError (for example, a custom registry missing a part) is plausibly reachable over REST. The max_concurrency, token_allowance and guard errors are reachable only from direct run_wiring callers with hand-written wirings.
evidence: scheduler.py:179, 190, 204 subclass ValueError; guards.py:31 subclasses ValueError; rest.py:250 registers a handler only for SeamRefusalError.
gui_impact: Operator sees generic 500 instead of 'node X has invalid max_concurrency'; no structured validation report.

description: Exceptions raised in the post-dispatch batch loop (meter() on malformed TokenAccounting fields, evaluate_guards when an output's __ne__ raises, NodeTrace construction) escape run_wiring as bare exceptions. That discards the traces of nodes that already completed in the batch, which contradicts the 'partial outcomes are never discarded' rule. The host() ValueError path is unreachable.
evidence: scheduler.py:430-433 catches only UnimplementedPlacementError/MissingWallClockCeilingError; 586 except* filter; 650-651 unguarded.
gui_impact: Rare 500 with an ExceptionGroup message and no trace_token for the run.

description: Nodes cancelled by TaskGroup because a sibling failed, and all nodes in later batches that were never scheduled, get no NodeTrace entry and no node_exceptions entry. The run record cannot distinguish 'not run' from 'not in wiring'.
evidence: scheduler.py:627-634 `continue` with no trace; 671-677 `break` leaves remaining nodes untraced.
gui_impact: Trace Inspector node table silently omits cancelled/unscheduled nodes; the GUI must diff against the wiring's node set (which it cannot fetch, no wiring route) to show them.

description: A failed node's wall_clock_ms is stamped 0 even though it ran (possibly until a subprocess timeout). Elapsed time before the failure is measured nowhere.
evidence: scheduler.py:467 start is local to _run_node and lost on raise; 603 `wall_clock_ms=0`.
gui_impact: Timing bar chart shows 0 ms for a node that may have consumed the full wall-clock ceiling.

description: Comment says a successful dispatch is always in-process and execution_mode is stamped on the trace via the refusal path. host() has accepted subprocess placement with a ceiling since 05-01, and NodeTrace has no execution_mode field; on refusal the placement exists only inside the cross_process_failure_cause string. The success path discards execution_mode (`_execution_mode`) and stamps cross_process_failure_cause=None with the comment 'in-process only'.
evidence: execution_mode.py:85-88 returns for subprocess with ceiling; trace.py:65-80 has no execution_mode; scheduler.py:638 `_execution_mode, output, wall_clock_ms = task.result()`; 664.
gui_impact: Operator cannot see which nodes ran in a subprocess (opaque nodes such as codebase-memory-mcp / lightrag full-ingest).

description: cache_hit is read from the body's return value, but no production part returns a `cache_hit` key; only the test part fake_llm_caller does. NodeTrace.cache_hit is therefore always False in production.
evidence: grep '"cache_hit"' under parts_core finds only parts_core/fake_llm_caller.py:63.
gui_impact: A cache_hit column would always read false; it should be hidden or labelled not reported.

description: Per-node max_concurrency semaphore is exposed as ctx._semaphore but no production part uses it, and no shipped wiring declares max_concurrency, so it is always 1 and unused.
evidence: grep '_semaphore' outside scheduler.py finds only tests/runner/test_scheduler.py:56; grep 'max_concurrency' in wirings/ and evidence/wirings/ finds nothing.
gui_impact: No concurrency control to expose; do not build a UI for it.

description: Engine stamps concurrency_setting='sequential' on every RunRecord, but the scheduler runs every ready batch concurrently in one TaskGroup. HippoRAG base has several dependency-free nodes (e.g. fact-score deps [] at wirings/hipporag/base.json:58-63) that run in parallel.
evidence: scheduler.py:571-585 creates one task per ready node; engine.py:257 `_CONCURRENCY_SETTING = "sequential"`; engine.py:620-625 says 'sequential' refers to arm order only.
gui_impact: Trace header shows 'sequential' for runs with intra-run parallelism; operator comparing determinism settings gets a misleading value.

description: determinism_setting and concurrency_setting are unused parameters of run_wiring, and the docstring's claim that they are 'threaded through' is misleading. The registry docstring is accurate.
evidence: No reference to registry/determinism_setting/concurrency_setting in the body 525-687; return dict 679-687 omits them.
gui_impact: none

description: split_allowance, apportion, ApportionmentPolicy, Allowance, BudgetHalted are used only by tests. Wirings carry `apportionment_policy` as free-text strings ('n/a - non-effectful join...') that nothing parses. BudgetState 'degraded' is never produced.
evidence: grep shows these symbols only in runner/budget.py and tests/runner/test_budget.py; wirings/hipporag/base.json:93 string value; meter returns only within_budget/halted (budget.py:138).
gui_impact: No fan-out budget split exists to visualise.

description: The trace omits the allowance and caps the share at 1.0, and stop_reason does not name the node. Spent is recoverable from tokens.prompt_tokens + completion_tokens, and for seam runs the allowance is the known 1,000,000 constant, so overspend can be computed client-side.
evidence: budget.py:118 `min(1.0, ...)`; trace.py:65-80 has no spent/allowance; scheduler.py:655.
gui_impact: Budget panel can show only a 0..1 bar; halted node must be found by scanning budget_state=='halted' with cross_process_failure_cause null.

description: Capability scoping is per store key, not per access mode: a node declaring only reads_kv receives the same writable raw kv handle as one declaring writes_kv. Read-only declaration does not prevent writes.
evidence: _ScopedStoresView.__getitem__ maps any effect whose suffix matches (272) and returns `self._scoped.require(effect)`; parts_core/__init__.py:64-71 returns `self._raw_stores[store_key]` unwrapped.
gui_impact: Effect badges ('reads_kv') overstate isolation; the operator cannot rely on them to know a node did not write.

description: max_concurrency and token_allowance go through int(), so True becomes 1, 2.7 becomes 2, 0.9 becomes 0 (halts any metered node with spend), and numeric strings like '100' are accepted silently.
evidence: scheduler.py:351 and 370 `int(raw)` with only TypeError/ValueError caught.
gui_impact: A future request-level token_allowance field would need its own validation.

description: Only HippoRAG ingest (a multi-node corpus wiring) is affected. An upstream node failure or budget halt surfaces as the synthetic 'ingest node produced no result and no exception' cause instead of the real exception recorded in node_exceptions. Delete is unaffected because HippoRAG has no delete wiring and LightRAG's delete wiring has one node.
evidence: engine.py:385 `scheduled.get("node_exceptions", {}).get(node_id)`; 388-392 synthetic RuntimeError; scheduler.py:599 keys by failing node.
gui_impact: Ingest/delete failure toast for HippoRAG shows a misleading cause; ingest/delete produce no trace to inspect instead.

description: run_wiring docstring lists the raising pre-flight cases as empty nodes, other parse violations, and max_concurrency below 1; it omits invalid token_allowance and guard declarations, which also raise pre-flight (538-544).
evidence: scheduler.py:521-523 vs 538-544.
gui_impact: none

description: CbmToolCallError raised inside the session is caught by the generic `except BaseException` and re-raised as CbmTransportError, so the documented distinction 'the RPC worked and the tool refused' vs 'the RPC failed' (docstring 141-144) never reaches any caller. CbmToolCallError is effectively dead as a raised type; no test covers it.
evidence: Only ForeignEngineUnavailableError is re-raised unchanged (245-246); everything else that is not TimeoutError becomes CbmTransportError (251-256). Reproduced with stubbed session returning is_error=True: output `CbmTransportError transport failure calling 'search_graph': codebase-memory-mcp tool 'search_graph' returned an error: bad arg (machine_endpoint=..., foreign_endpoint=...)`. grep of databasise/tests shows no CbmToolCallError assertion.
gui_impact: If this engine is ever wired, a bad tool argument would be shown as a transport/placement failure; the console could not tell user error from a dead process.

description: The wall-clock ceiling covers only the tool call. Process launch and `session.initialize()` run outside `anyio.fail_after(timeout)`, so a binary that starts but never completes the MCP handshake blocks the worker thread with no bound, violating the §8 condition 4 ceiling the docstring claims (113-116, 278-280).
evidence: `await session.initialize()` at line 242 precedes `with anyio.fail_after(timeout):` at line 243. Callers run it via asyncio.to_thread (parts_core/codebase_memory_mcp.py:309), so the hang also pins a thread.
gui_impact: A request using this part could hang indefinitely with no timeout refusal.

description: CorpusOpSubprocessError keeps the first 2000 characters of stderr (`stderr.strip()[:2000]`). v1 logs to stderr (SafeStreamHandler, v1/lightrag/utils.py:62,94) and the traceback with the actual exception line is printed last (driver 353-355), so on any run that logs more than ~2000 chars before failing the message, and therefore ForeignEngineRefusalError.cause (seam/refusals.py:489-501), contains only log lines and not the exception.
evidence: Line 64 slices from the head. main() prints the traceback at the end of stderr (v1_corpus_driver_script.py:353-355). ForeignEngineRefusalError message embeds str(cause) (refusals.py:499-501).
gui_impact: The 'cause' field the console shows for failed ingest/delete may not name the failure. Tail truncation (`[-2000:]`) would fix it.

description: Raw v1 stderr (tracebacks, log lines, file paths, request URLs/model hosts from openai client errors) is carried into ForeignEngineRefusalError.cause and returned to the HTTP/MCP caller. PLAUSIBLE: whether any secret value appears depends on v1/openai exception text.
evidence: CorpusOpSubprocessError message includes stderr (64); ForeignEngineRefusalError includes str(cause) (500); inventory documents `cause: str` in the 422 body (API-INVENTORY.md:340).
gui_impact: Console should render cause in a collapsed, operator-only panel; the API should not expose it to non-operator consumers.

description: Each call spawns an independent v1 process against the same working_dir with no cross-process lock. v1's storage locks are in-process. Two concurrent ingests, or an ingest plus a delete, each load the JSON KV/doc-status/graph files at start and write at finalize_storages, so one run's writes can overwrite the other's. PLAUSIBLE (not reproduced; depends on the backends set in v1/.env.parity, which was not read).
evidence: grep -n 'Lock' databasise/seam/engine.py finds no lock around ingest/delete; run_corpus_op uses subprocess.run per call (134-142); driver builds a fresh facade per op (183, 206) and finalizes at the end (194, 210). Default v1 backends are JsonKVStorage/JsonDocStatusStorage/NetworkXStorage/NanoVectorDBStorage (v1/env.example:817-820).
gui_impact: Console must serialize LightRAG ingest/delete (one write in flight) until the engine adds a lock.

description: A timed-out ingest leaves the document persisted as PARSING/ANALYZING/PROCESSING. No status field or route reports it as orphaned, and no explicit retry route exists. The next ingest of any document resets interrupted and FAILED documents to PENDING as a side effect and reprocesses them inside that request's run.
evidence: timeout=INGEST_WALL_CLOCK_CEILING_SECONDS (full_ingest.py:218-223); TimeoutExpired -> CorpusOpTimeoutError (143-144); v1 recovery only runs inside apipeline_process_enqueue_documents.
gui_impact: Corpus view will show documents stuck in 'processing' with no job in flight; console needs a 'stuck' indicator and a retry/reprocess action that does not exist.

description: json.loads at v1_corpus_adapter.py:149 is unguarded, so non-JSON stdout would raise JSONDecodeError, but no stdout writer on the driver paths is known (the cited print is not on the path). On status/job routes every adapter failure, named or not, is an unmapped 500. On ingest/delete every failure is wrapped as ForeignEngineRefusalError.
evidence: Line 149 `return json.loads(proc.stdout)` with no try; docstring 9-11 claims every failure is a named refusal.
gui_impact: Unstructured 500s on corpus/job routes.

description: `storages_initialized` is a constant True on every exit-0 path; it carries no information beyond the exit code. `working_dir_present` is computed before _build_rag, and LightRAG's constructor creates the directory (v1/lightrag/lightrag.py:1004), so the read-only health probe mutates disk and the field is false only on the very first call.
evidence: Lines 323-326: `rag = await _build_rag(...)` then `storages_initialized = True`; line 321 checks existence before construction.
gui_impact: Health panel fields are near-useless; the real cause of degraded health is discarded (engine.py:954-956 catches all exceptions).

description: limit/offset are trusted from the job; a negative limit slices `document_ids[offset:offset+limit]` and returns up to total-1 entries, bypassing MAX_PAGE_SIZE. Page validator only checks limit > MAX_PAGE_SIZE and offset < 0 (seam/corpus.py:133-138). (Already noted in the inventory.)
evidence: corpus.py:136 `if self.limit > MAX_PAGE_SIZE`; no lower bound. Driver line 301.
gui_impact: GUI must clamp limit to 1..100.

description: v1/.env.parity values override the process environment. A missing file is silently treated as empty. If the process environment does not supply the v1 variables, every driver run fails with a KeyError traceback, surfacing as ForeignEngineRefusalError on ingest/delete, a bare 500 on status/job routes, and 'degraded' with no reason on health. No named 'v1 not configured' refusal exists.
evidence: Lines 123-125; _load_env_file returns {} for absent file (86-87).
gui_impact: Health shows 'degraded' with no reason when v1 is unconfigured; console cannot display effective v1 config.

description: Tool admissibility is checked only after the call. The part body passes any ctx.config['tool'] straight to call_tool, then normalise_to_item_kind raises UntypedForeignItemError for mutating tools (e.g. delete_project, index_repository, manage_adr). The mutation has already executed when the refusal is raised.
evidence: codebase_memory_mcp.py:309-316 calls call_tool before normalising; adapter 314-315 raises only in normalise. Wiring declares effects mutates_store (wirings/codebase-memory-mcp.json).
gui_impact: If wired, a refused request could still have deleted or re-indexed a project.

description: CONTRACT §4 (docs/system-model/CONTRACT.md:270) requires derived_finding to carry `derived_from: [Ref]` and forbids kind as a bare scalar. The adapter emits `kind` as a plain string and `derived_from` as a synthetic string `cbm-project:<project or tool_name>`, which falls back to the tool name when no project is echoed, so it names no evidence.
evidence: Lines 340-341 and 345; module comment 60-64 admits no ItemKind type exists.
gui_impact: Evidence inspector cannot dereference derived_from for this engine.

description: import_real_mcp mutates the global sys.path without a lock. This is a latent race only: the threaded call path (CBM call_tool) is unreachable from REST/MCP, and the MCP server calls it single-threaded at import time.
evidence: sys.path[:] reassignment at 113 and restore at 117 with no lock; call path parts_core/codebase_memory_mcp.py:309 uses asyncio.to_thread.
gui_impact: Intermittent import errors under concurrent load; low.

description: ops 'entities' and 'entity_info' (per-document entity contribution and post-delete survival) are implemented but only tests call them; no engine method, REST route or MCP tool reaches them.
evidence: grep of non-test code for run_corpus_op calls shows only 'ingest', 'delete', 'status', 'health' (engine.py:863-950, full_ingest.py:220, full_delete.py:220).
gui_impact: Delete-impact preview is impossible through the API although the driver supports it.

description: Stale docstrings at v1_corpus_adapter.py:5 and v1_corpus_driver_script.py:112-113 describe delete/status as future work. foreign/__init__.py:4-5 is accurate. f07_report.py:46-48 wrongly claims an existing unlink shape in the CBM adapter.
evidence: Cited lines; grep result empty.
gui_impact: none

description: When every measured excursion lacks a cause, render_deviations_document passes an empty `reasoned` list to render_deviations_markdown. That function then prints the completed-run 'Zero declared deviations ... a completed comparison that found no excursion' paragraph, and the 'Outstanding' section listing the pending excursions is appended after it. The same document states both that no excursion was found and that N excursions are pending. The `else` branch also catches run state 'mixed', which is not a completed run.
evidence: Reproduced: render_deviations_document([DeclaredDeviation(arm='hybrid',query_id='q1',description='chunk_diff: x',cause='',field='chunk_diff')]) emits headings ['## Zero declared deviations' (text: 'completed comparison that found no excursion'), '## Known design deviation (pending measurement)', '## Outstanding — CONTRACT §5 cause not yet recorded']. The committed file avoids this only because the two naive causes exist.
gui_impact: A GUI that renders or parses DECLARED-DEVIATIONS.md cannot use the 'Zero declared deviations' heading as a status signal. Compute the deviation status from parity_results plus human_findings.json.

description: Internal-rule violation, not a CONTRACT violation: parity_report.py documents human_findings.json as human-authored and says an executor cannot author causes (42-45, 90-92, 502-503), yet both committed causes are AI-recorded (human_findings.json:11,22) and the renderer accepts them without checking recorded_by (679-683). CONTRACT.md:308 only requires deviations to be named explicitly. The deviations table shows recorded_by; the PARITY-EVIDENCE Verdict (1307-1313) does not.
evidence: human_findings.json recorded_by: "Claude (AI agent, gsd-code-fixer) — commit 2ce3c30; NOT recorded by the human owner, despite this file's own name". _collect_deviations:679-683 copies cause and recorded_by with no provenance check.
gui_impact: A deviations view must show recorded_by prominently and must not treat 'Named' as owner-approved. A GUI form that records causes would need to stamp the real operator identity.

description: _run_state() returns 'completed', 'inconclusive' or 'mixed', but the prose branches test only `== 'completed'`. A mixed state therefore renders the inconclusive text: 'v1/.venv ... v1/.env.parity are all absent', 'Every arm above reports matched=0 no-touch=0 over-declared=0', and 'Every one of the five arms ... reports an environment-precondition refusal'. These statements are false when some arms completed.
evidence: _run_state:122-126 returns 'mixed' for any status set other than {completed} or {inconclusive}. _render_what_was_compared:860 sets completed = state == 'completed'. _render_storage_audit:1144 and _render_verdict:1285 use the same binary test.
gui_impact: If the GUI shows parity status, derive it per arm from the result files, not from the rendered prose.

description: parity_report.py violates its own comment at 103-104 ('no section may assert a run state it did not read'), not the purity statement in the docstring: the naive verdict (1306-1313) is a fixed literal and miscounts (one excursion per query, of 2 and 4 chunks), the corpus size (954) is a literal, the heading '(pending measurement)' (542) persists after the status sentence says the deviation was measured, and the elif at 581-598 claims 'non-empty on every query' without checking each query.
evidence: The current committed DECLARED-DEVIATIONS.md:12 reads '(pending measurement)' and :16 reads 'does surface as a measured excursion'. The elif branch at 581-598 also says diffs are 'non-empty on every query' without checking each query.
gui_impact: Do not scrape these documents for status. Read the JSON.

description: _render_answer_spotcheck keys spot-checks by query_id only, so a second entry for the same query (for example a different arm) silently overwrites the first. The AnswerSpotCheck schema carries `arm`, which implies more than one per query is valid.
evidence: by_query[spotcheck.query_id] = spotcheck (line 799); QUERY_IDS loop at 820 renders one entry per query.
gui_impact: A spot-check entry form would lose data per arm. Key on (query_id, arm) or refuse duplicates.

description: _render_spotcheck_arm_guidance says 'All five arms completed without a decomposed-run degradation' but checks only hybrid/local/global for degradation. naive and bypass are never checked.
evidence: graph_arms = ('hybrid','local','global') at 765; blocked_arms is computed only over graph_arms.
gui_impact: Minor. Determine per-arm availability from each arm's own degraded flag.

description: check_results says it 'never raises for a validation failure', but a malformed JSON file raises JSONDecodeError (247, 286) and a declared_causes entry with no 'field' key raises a bare KeyError (645). These are not named ProvenanceViolation or refusal errors.
evidence: json.loads(...) is not wrapped. The dict comprehension at 644-646 indexes entry['arm'], entry['query_id'], entry['field'] directly.
gui_impact: If a GUI ever writes human_findings.json, it must validate the shape itself, because the renderer crashes on a missing key and gives no named refusal.

description: Named-deviation table rows insert description, cause, recorded_by and recorded_at without _escape_cell, although _escape_cell exists (851) and is used elsewhere. A human-authored cause that contains '|' or a newline breaks the Markdown table.
evidence: f"| {d.arm} | {d.query_id} | {d.description} | {d.cause} | ..." with no escaping.
gui_impact: Free-text cause entry from a GUI could corrupt the rendered record. Escape or reject '|' and newlines.

description: The Falsifier 2 verdict paragraph is a fixed string that asserts every probe 'fired with its expected code, each paired with a control that did not fire'. It does not read the probe results that _render_probe_table computes. If a probe stopped firing, the table would say 'DID NOT FIRE' while the verdict still said 'Falsifier 2 did not fire ... D4's brake holds'.
evidence: render_markdown appends the verdict unconditionally after _render_probe_table(). Probe outcomes are not passed in. All 7 probes currently match (verified by running evaluate_probe), so the committed document is accurate today.
gui_impact: If the GUI shows Falsifier 2 status, compute it from evaluate_probe results, not the verdict text.

description: probe_registry's docstring says the production default_registry() 'stays exactly D-04's seven entries', and the rendered text says wirings are resolved against default_registry()'s 'Phase-1 entries'. The live default_registry() holds 35 parts.

The same module's reason text (39-46) says codebase-memory-mcp is not resolvable through any production selector. Measured: none of the six all_wirings() candidates (naive, bypass, hybrid, local, global, hipporag) contains mutates_store, so the MutableStoreComparisonExcludedError branch in Databasise.compare can never fire from REST /compare or the MCP compare tool.

description: The F-07 record says 'MODAL-05 itself stays unproven ... (the owner-deferred real cross-modality run)'. CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md's appended 2026-09-10 section says 'MODAL-05 is **discharged**' (line 253), while that file's own title (line 1) and Status section (line 14) still say 'BLOCKED, Not Discharged'.

description: w2's boundary knob rationale says cbm 'can be run once consuming machine-produced chunks and once chunking natively'. FALSIFIER-4-EVIDENCE.md records the machine-chunk leg as not runnable, because index_repository accepts only repo_path. This rationale is rendered into FALSIFIER-2-EVIDENCE.md as a §19.10 boundary row.

description: The A/A driver measures an index that the eval-corpus ingest never populates for the default arm. corpus_ingest defaults to --arm lightrag, whose corpus wiring is the opaque lightrag/full-ingest node; that node calls run_corpus_op without working_dir, so v1 writes into v1/.corpus_working_dir, not into the engine's store_root v1/.eval_corpus_store. aa_run then calls engine.query(QueryObject(text=...)) with no selector, which resolves to the default LightRAG naive arm reading the v2 Faiss 'chunks' namespace under v1/.eval_corpus_store. aa_run has no --arm option, so the HippoRAG arm (the only arm whose ingest writes into store_root) cannot be selected.
evidence: full_ingest.py:219-224 `await asyncio.to_thread(run_corpus_op, "ingest", payload, timeout=...)` (no working_dir); v1_corpus_adapter.py:129 `"working_dir": str(working_dir or DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR)`, :31 DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = v1/.corpus_working_dir; aa_run.py:366 `await engine.query(QueryObject(text=question.text))`; selectors.py:241 no-selector path -> _resolve_default (naive arm first, selectors.py:210-214); aa_run.py:522-528 argparse has no arm flag. Consequence: gold_passage scoring sees empty evidence, score_gold_passage returns 0.0 for every question in both passes (aa_run.py:238-239), all diffs are 0, and calibrate_aa_floor returns a floor of 0.0 that looks valid.
gui_impact: Any floor a console displays from this driver would be a measurement of an empty index; the console should not present aa_run output as a calibrated floor until the driver selects an arm and the ingest lands in the same store.

description: The comment is not false about the two named stores. It is misleading because it calls _EVAL_INGEST_STORE_ROOT the store this path ingests into: for the default lightrag arm, eval documents go to the repo-wide v1/.corpus_working_dir, never to v1/.eval_corpus_store, and that directory backs GET /corpus and /corpus/counts on every instance.

description: The §AA.2 cache-bypass precondition cannot fail in a real run. (a) _verify_cache_bypassed iterates the node lists and passes when they are empty, so a pass that yields no node traces calibrates without any bypass evidence. (b) The scheduler coerces an unreported cache flag to False via bool(output.get('cache_hit')), so every real trace node carries an explicit False and the 'unknown status' refusal branch is unreachable; only parts_core/fake_llm_caller.py:48-63 ever reports cache_hit. The module docstring (calibration.py:20-23) says an unknown bypass status is a refusal.
evidence: Reproduced: calibrate_aa_floor([0.0,0.1,-0.1,0.0], identity=..., run_a_nodes=[], run_b_nodes=[], seed=1) returned floor 0.05 with no error. scheduler.py:403 `cache_hit = bool(output.get("cache_hit"))`; scheduler.py:406 `cache_hit = False` for non-mapping output. grep for cache_hit in parts_core finds only fake_llm_caller.py.
gui_impact: A console must not label a floor as 'cache-bypass verified'; the engine has no real evidence of bypass.

description: open_sealed copies the old version's splits unchanged into a new version and writes the 'sealed_open' usage entry only to the new version. The old version keeps an empty usage log with no record that its sealed partition was exposed. A later mint_bundle with the same inputs dedups by content hash to the lowest matching version, which is the old one, so callers get a version that looks unopened. The new version's 'sealed' split is the same already-opened question set, so it is not sealed either. aa_run's default version (max number) picks the opened copy.
evidence: Reproduced in a temp root: mint -> bundle@v1; open_sealed(v1) -> bundle@v2 with identical sealed ids (True); mint_bundle again returns bundle@v1; bundle@v1/usage.jsonl is ''. bundle.py:502-506 copies content and appends usage to new_version only; _find_version_by_content_hash iterates ascending (bundle.py:228).
gui_impact: A bundle audit view built from usage.jsonl would show the original version as clean after its sealed set was read; the console needs to show the opening on both versions or flag same-content_hash siblings.

description: The version identity hash covers question ids, gold answers, judge, corpus_snapshot_hash and the settings, but not question text and not gold_document_ids (the gold_passage family's targets). snapshot.corpus_hash covers documents only; the query set has a separate queries_hash that is not included. Editing a question's text or its gold document ids while keeping ids and answers makes mint_bundle return the old version, whose stored question texts and gold-passage targets are stale.
evidence: bundle.py:215-223 payload keys; parity/corpus.py:100-102 corpus_hash = sha256 of document digests only; parity/corpus.py:111-119 queries_hash is separate and is not passed to _compute_content_hash; bundle.py:373-375 returns existing version on hash match.
gui_impact: A bundle list keyed by content_hash would show 'unchanged' after a gold-target edit.

description: The floor is the upper percentile of the signed mean of run_b - run_a. When the two A/A passes differ systematically in one direction (pass order effect, warm caches, rate limiting), the floor is negative and a zero or negative candidate delta clears it. The null is not symmetrised (no absolute value, no two-sided bound).
evidence: Reproduced: calibrate_aa_floor([-0.2,-0.3,-0.25,-0.2], ...) -> floor -0.2; clears_floor(0.0) -> True.
gui_impact: A console showing 'clears floor' must also show the floor value and sign.

UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError is caught, as a SeamRefusalError subclass.

description: score_gold_passage reads record['document_id'] from the resolved vector metadata. Only hipporag/chunker-embedder writes a document_id key (parts_core/hipporag/chunk_embed.py:84). LightRAG chunk metadata imported from v1 (parity/import_index.py:179-191) carries v1's own keys, not document_id, so a gold_passage pass against a populated LightRAG store raises KeyError (uncaught, EVAL-07).

description: Reusing the clients across per-family asyncio.run calls makes the first request of the second family hit a pooled connection bound to the closed loop. The openai SDK's default retries normally recover by opening a new connection. Only when retries are exhausted does it surface, as openai.APIConnectionError (cause: RuntimeError 'Event loop is closed'), which main does not catch.
evidence: aa_run.py:566 `asyncio.run(calibrate_family(...))` inside `for family_name in families`; openai_compat.py:112 `self._client = ... openai.AsyncOpenAI(`. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE, not executed (requires live endpoints).
gui_impact: none directly; affects the default two-family CLI run.

CorpusDriftError (load_snapshot), MissingTargetFamilyError, BundleDriftError (dedup loads each existing version) and client network errors escape as tracebacks. _REPO_EVAL_DIR (line 50) is the databasise package dir, not an eval dir.

location: databasise/seam/corpus.py:134-140 (Page._bounded), reached from databasise/mcp/server.py:111-123 and databasise/seam/rest.py:185-203, 342, 361; slicing at databasise/foreign/v1_corpus_driver_script.py:301
description: Page refuses limit > 100 and offset < 0 but never checks limit < 1. A negative limit passes both _checked_page copies (MCP and REST) and the driver slices document_ids[offset:offset+limit], so limit=-1 returns all but the last document: the MAX_PAGE_SIZE bound is bypassed. limit=0 returns zero documents and next_offset == offset, so a paging client loops.
evidence: Page._bounded checks only `self.limit > MAX_PAGE_SIZE` and `self.offset < 0` (corpus.py:136-139). REST declares `limit: int = Query(default=50)` with no ge (rest.py:342, 361). StatusToolArgs.limit is a bare int (tools.py:160). Driver: `page_ids = document_ids[offset : offset + limit]` (v1_corpus_driver_script.py:301). engine.corpus_status next_offset = page.offset + len(documents) (engine.py:895).
gui_impact: Corpus/job list views must validate 1 <= limit <= 100 client-side; a bad value returns an unbounded list or an endless pager.

description: MCP: AmbiguousIngestPayloadError, OversizedDocumentError and the negative-offset ValueError are wrapped in pydantic ValidationError and surface as UnexpectedToolError 'Error executing tool <name>' with no reason. REST does not map them either. POST /documents gives FastAPI's generic 422 validation body, not the refusal shape. POST /documents/upload with an oversized file gives an unhandled 500 (rest.py:328-332; the try/except at 333-336 covers only the selector parse).
evidence: Live: IngestToolArgs(text='a', raw_base64='YQ==').to_ingest_document() raises pydantic_core.ValidationError. call_tool('ingest', {'args': {'text':'a','raw_base64':'YQ=='}}) -> UnexpectedToolError 'Error executing tool ingest'. call_tool('status', {'args': {'scope':'corpus','offset':-1}}) -> UnexpectedToolError 'Error executing tool status'. SDK: mcp/server/mcpserver/tools/base.py:158 drops the message for non-ToolError exceptions.
gui_impact: None for the REST GUI. Any MCP-based operator tool receives no reason for these refusals.

description: The docstring says server.call_tool re-raises the tool's own ToolError directly. In mcp 2.2.0 it wraps it again as ToolError(f'Error executing tool {name}: {exc}'), so the refusal text a client sees is 'Error executing tool resolve: {json}', not a JSON string.
evidence: SDK .venv/.../mcp/server/mcpserver/tools/base.py:153 `raise ToolError(f"Error executing tool {self.name}: {exc}") from exc`. Live: call_tool('resolve', {'args': {'scope':'trace','trace_reference':'nope'}}) -> ToolError 'Error executing tool resolve: {"refusal_type": "UnknownTraceReferenceError", ...}'.
gui_impact: An MCP client must remove the prefix before parsing the JSON refusal.

gui_impact: none for REST; corrupted MCP uploads ingest silently

description: chat() takes choices[0].message.content without checking it. It raises IndexError on an empty choices list, and can return None (for a tool-call or refusal response) into ChatResult.text: str. embed() does not check that len(response.data) == len(texts), and it does not reorder by item.index, so the one-vector-per-input-in-order guarantee in EmbeddingResult (base.py:37-38) is assumed, not enforced.
evidence: `text = response.choices[0].message.content` (131); `vectors = [item.embedding for item in response.data]` (149).
gui_impact: Possible unnamed node failures or mis-bound vectors show up only as partial runs with opaque stop_reason.

description: environment_hash includes platform.platform() (kernel release and glibc version), which the env.py docstring does not mention. A host kernel or glibc update therefore changes every config_hash and instance_hash computed by the scheduler. Seam store namespaces are fixed names and are not affected, and cache_partition_key is used only by the fake LLM test part.

gui_impact: After a reboot into a new kernel the operator sees new identities and cache misses with no explanation; no route exposes the environment digest or what changed.

description: PLAUSIBLE, not reproduced here: if any installed distribution's RECORD contains '/nix/store/' (for example Python packages supplied by Nix instead of uv), environment_hash raises EnvironmentDigestError. That aborts every scheduler run, and the health route does not check for it.
evidence: _assert_no_nix_store_path(record_text, ...) at env.py:55; environment_hash() called unguarded at runner/scheduler.py:324; Databasise.health (engine.py:916-963) does not call it.
gui_impact: Every query would fail while /health reports ok.

description: gc_namespace has no production caller, so CONTRACT §3's 'GC'd with the instance that produced it' for quarantined namespaces never happens. It also passes ignore_errors=True, which swallows failures and contradicts the refusals-over-silent-fallbacks rule. The docstring says the one-directory-per-namespace layout is 'baked into every namespace-derivation call site', but the seam stores use fixed names (chunks, hipporag-chunks), and derive_namespace is called only by parity/import_index.py.
evidence: grep gc_namespace: namespaces.py and tests only; grep derive_namespace: parity/import_index.py only; namespace_dir: stores/blob.py only.
gui_impact: No namespace listing or GC operation exists to expose; disk growth from quarantined artifacts is unmanaged.

description: scan_tree rglobs the whole databasise/ directory, including .venv/site-packages: 4323 of the 4576 files scanned are third-party, and a run takes about 11 s. Any dependency file that imports a top-level module named lightrag or v1, or contains a '../v1/' literal, gives a false violation, and any file that does not parse under the running interpreter crashes the check. Dynamic imports through `from importlib import import_module; import_module('lightrag')` are not detected (only `importlib.import_module` attribute form, 98-104). The docstring (35-36) says subprocess exclusions match by resolved path, but the code matches by bare filename (154).
evidence: Live: files scanned 4576, in .venv 4323, exit 0, real 0m10.99s.
gui_impact: none

If the scheduler raises, the SqliteKVStore is never finalized. canonicalise(wiring_doc) runs after execution, so a wiring with an integer outside int64 executes fully and only then raises CanonicalisationError, with no run record returned.

description: databasise.tools has an __init__.py but is not listed in packages, so an installed wheel omits check_import_boundary. The version string is held in three places: pyproject.toml:7, __init__.py:38 and rest.py:248 FastAPI(version="0.1.0"). rest.py does not import __version__, so these can drift. The mcp extra has no upper bound (mcp>=2.2.0) although server.py depends on the 2.x-specific MCPServer name (server.py:6-11).

description: Admission records for all three opaque parts state that §8 conditions 7, 10 and 11 are 'enforced by databasise.parts.admission.cross_check_conditions at registration time'. PartRegistry.register calls only validate_admission; cross_check_conditions has no production caller (only tests/parts/test_admission.py). Conditions 7, 10, 11 are therefore not machine-checked when the engine starts.

gui_impact: An admission panel that displays these verdicts would present as enforced checks that never run. Either wire cross_check_conditions into default_registry() or reword the evidence.

description: Registration gates admission on kind == 'opaque', but ForbiddenSharedScopeError checks structural_depth == 'opaque'. A part with kind='opaque', structural_depth='stage', artifact_scope='shared' passes registration, although §8 condition 5 forbids an opaque node writing the shared scope.

Effects outside the 17-member Effect literal are accepted. cross_check_conditions' condition-11 test `"as_of" in registered_part.effects` (admission.py:545) relies on this unvalidated list.

description: The artifact registry and its D-02 second blast-radius call site are never used by the running engine. No part body, runner or engine method calls write_artifact or ArtifactRegistry; parts that declare writes_artifact (lightrag/full-ingest@0.1.0, lightrag/embedder-index@0.1.0, hipporag/graph-materializer@0.1.0) produce no registry rows. ArtifactRegistry.overlaps has no caller at all, test or production.

An invalid scope or retention tier writes an unreferenced blob and then raises raw sqlite3.IntegrityError from the CHECK constraint.
