description: UnbudgetableParticipantError cannot be reached on /query, /query/stream or /compare with the shipped OpenAICompatibleClient. lightrag/full-ingest (conditionally, full_ingest.py:238) and lightrag/full-delete (always, full_delete.py:239) set the sentinel, but they run only via ingest()/delete_document(), which never call assemble_token_breakdown. The HippoRAG query wiring's openie and entity-fact-embed nodes pass the sentinel on from any client that reports it, so an injected client can trigger the refusal on a HippoRAG run. codebase_memory_mcp reports counted_by 'none', not 'unbudgetable'.
evidence: grep for 'unbudgetable' in parts_core finds only those three. engine.py:652-851 (ingest/delete) has no assemble_token_breakdown call.
gui_impact: The inventory lists it as a live /query and /compare refusal. A GUI state for it is harmless but untestable against the real engine.

description: stop_reason and degradation_reason carry the internal node id, which §18.2 forbids on the envelope. The redaction gate (seam/redact.py) is never called at runtime. Only tests import it, so nothing strips or blocks the leak.
evidence: Live probe: POST /query {query:{text:'x'}} returned stop_reason "node 'embedder-query': NodeExecutionError: declared effect 'calls_embedding' requires client 'embedding', but no client is wired under that key for this run". `grep assert_no_forbidden|forbidden_identities` finds only tests/seam/test_{leak,trace_token,compare,rest_transport}.py and seam/redact.py itself.
gui_impact: The GUI shows internal node ids in partial-run banners. If this is fixed later, stop_reason text will change, so the GUI must not parse it.

description: If the declared evidence_position node returns a dict without an 'items' key, `retrieval_output["items"]` raises KeyError, which surfaces as an unstructured 500. It does not refuse and does not yield empty evidence.
evidence: `retrieval_items = retrieval_output["items"] if isinstance(retrieval_output, dict) else []`. The dict branch indexes without .get(). The current chunk-vector and assemble-result parts do return 'items' (parts_core/hipporag/assemble_result.py:67), so this is latent.
gui_impact: A future part shape will cause a generic 500 on /query instead of an empty evidence list.

description: Comparison keys can collide across selector kinds. Alias 'default' collides with the default selector. Alias 'a+b' collides with capability ['a','b']. Harness 'x' collides with alias 'x'. A collision refuses only after the earlier arms have run and persisted traces. Separately, with 2+ selectors a key literally named 'answer' (an alias named 'answer') breaks the inventory's rule of telling the response shape apart by an `answer` key.
evidence: render_selector_key returns the alias or harness string unchanged and joins capability lists with '+'. Live probe: selectors [{},{}] gives DuplicateComparisonKeyError {key:'default'} after the first arm ran.
gui_impact: The client-side duplicate-key preview must use the same rendering rule across all kinds. The GUI should decide between one envelope and a keyed map from the number of selectors it sent, not from the presence of an `answer` key.

description: The query.py docstring (lines 22-25) says registering a part that declares the matching capability will make embedding, predicates, profile_ref or formal_query consumable. That cannot happen: the required capabilities ('reads_space', 'predicate-query', 'profile-ref-resolution', 'formal-query-language') are not members of the frozen 17-member Effect literal, and Part.effects is typed list[Effect]. Those four members stay refused unless the frozen Effect vocabulary changes.
evidence: Effect literal at schema.py:31-49 contains none of the four strings. `effects: list[Effect]` at schema.py:137 and 160. check_consumable compares against the union of part.effects (query.py:63-69).
gui_impact: The 'advanced members' panel can show these four as permanently disabled. They will not become available just because a part is registered.

description: promote() derives the arm from the set of node ids that have a NodeTrace. A partial run traces only the nodes that were dispatched (scheduler.py:574-664 breaks after a failing batch), so the set matches no wiring and an AssertionError gives an unstructured 500.
evidence: Live probe: a HippoRAG partial run trace (debug) holds only [('chunk-embed','within_budget'), ('fact-score','halted')]. hipporag has 13 nodes, so _arm_name_for_node_ids raises AssertionError, which is not a SeamRefusalError.
gui_impact: The inventory's chained 'promote from this result' on /query and 'promote this arm' on /compare must be disabled when the envelope has partial:true.

description: ForbiddenSelectorInputError is raised inside a pydantic model_validator (selectors.py:113-127), so FastAPI reports it as a validation 422 with no refusal_type field, and the at-most-one-member rule raises a plain ValueError (selectors.py:107-110). Both arrive as {detail:[{type:'value_error', loc:[...], msg:'Value error, ...', ctx:{error:...}}]}. The GUI must classify them by loc plus ctx.error keys. Most refusal messages, not just this one, lack a class-name prefix; refusal 422s carry the name in refusal_type.
evidence: Live probe, hash-shaped alias: {detail:[{type:'value_error', loc:['body','selector'], msg:"Value error, selector member 'alias' carries a value shaped like an internal identity: '...'", ctx:{error:{member_name:'alias', value:'...'}}}]}. Multi-member: ctx:{error:{}}. On /compare, loc is ['body','selectors',<index>].
gui_impact: The GUI cannot recover refusal_type for selector errors. It must map them by loc and ctx.error keys (member_name/value present means hash-shaped).

description: Both 2.0 transports exist only as factories. Nothing launches either. No [project.scripts], no __main__ module in databasise/seam or databasise/mcp, no uvicorn.run call, no MCPServer.run call, and no MCP client config in the repo.
evidence: A grep for 'uvicorn', 'create_app(', 'create_server(' and 'stdio' across databasise/ (excluding tests) finds only pyproject.toml:84 (the dependency) and the two def lines (rest.py:235, server.py:177). A live check shows create_server(...) has run, run_stdio_async, run_sse_async and run_streamable_http_async, and nothing calls them. No .mcp.json exists at the repo root.
gui_impact: The console cannot connect until a launcher exists. The launcher must take store_root, workspace, host, port and clients. For MCP, it must also choose stdio, SSE or streamable-HTTP.

description: For --arm lightrag (the default), corpus_ingest --spend ingests into v1/.corpus_working_dir through run_corpus_op's default working_dir. That is the same v1 directory the REST /documents route and /corpus use. It does not write v1/.eval_corpus_store, which the comment at corpus_ingest.py:67-68 names as the target. aa_run (aa_run.py:554-562, 366) then queries the lightrag-base default wiring, an 18-node KG+vector wiring and not 'naive', over v2 namespaces under .eval_corpus_store/eval-corpus-ingest. full-ingest never writes those namespaces, so the chained LightRAG ingest-then-calibrate workflow cannot retrieve anything. The HippoRAG arm does write v2 stores under .eval_corpus_store.
evidence: full_ingest.py:219-224 calls run_corpus_op('ingest', payload, timeout=...) with no working_dir. v1_corpus_adapter.py:129 sets working_dir to str(working_dir or DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR). aa_run.py:357 calls engine.query(QueryObject(text=question.text)) with no selector. v1/.eval_corpus_store does not exist on disk today (ls).
gui_impact: An eval 'ingest' button for the LightRAG arm would also change the operator's live corpus list (/corpus reads v1/.corpus_working_dir). A following A/A run would refuse with ConfoundedPassError or score zero. Do not offer these as a chained workflow.

description: The import_index CLI has no argparse. It checks only for the literal '--verify' in argv and ignores every other argument. `--help`, or a misspelling such as `--verfiy`, runs a full import_v1_index into v1/.parity_v2_store before verifying.
evidence: import_index.py:504-511: `argv = sys.argv[1:] ...; verify_only = "--verify" in argv; ... if not verify_only: await import_v1_index(DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR, DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT)`.
gui_impact: A console button must pass the exact argument '--verify' for a read-only verification. Any other argument mutates the only populated v2 store.

description: Unknown `--query` ids are filtered out silently. The run then completes with zero records, overwrites parity/.comparison_results/<arm>.json with [] and exits 0.
evidence: _run_cli at run_comparison.py:678-682 does `queries = tuple(q for q in queries if q.id in wanted)` and does not check for an empty result. main at run_comparison.py:726-736 writes `json.dumps([r.to_dict() for r in records])` and returns 0 when there is no error and no inconclusive record.
gui_impact: A console parity button that passes a free-text query id can erase earlier comparison results and show the run as successful. The console must validate ids against the snapshot's queries.

description: render_markdown always appends '**Result: Falsifier 2 did not fire.** ... every self-declaration and blast-radius refusal probe fired with its expected code'. This happens even when _render_probe_table produced 'DID NOT FIRE' or 'UNEXPECTED VIOLATION' rows. main() then overwrites the committed FALSIFIER-2-EVIDENCE.md and exits with no status code.
evidence: falsifier2.py:476-480 computes per-probe verdict strings. falsifier2.py:540-552 appends the verdict paragraph unconditionally. main() at falsifier2.py:558-561 returns None, so the exit code is always 0.
gui_impact: A console that shows this report must read the probe table, not the verdict sentence or the exit code.

description: The two CLIs catch only MissingParityEnvError. MissingParityEnvKeyError and UnparseableProviderRoutingError, both raised by _build_clients (run_arm.py:174-176, 135-136), escape as tracebacks. The sibling CLIs eval.corpus_ingest, eval.aa_run and parity.build_hipporag_index do catch MissingParityEnvKeyError.
evidence: run_arm.py:356-360 is `except MissingParityEnvError`. storage_audit.py:241-245 is `except _run_arm.MissingParityEnvError`.
gui_impact: A console wrapper must treat non-zero exit with stderr as the failure signal. It cannot rely on a one-line message.

description: Both module docstrings say the module 'has not been invoked for real in this environment'. CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md records a refused real run and a completed real run on 2026-09-10 (MODAL-05 discharged), and the hipporag-* namespaces exist on disk.
evidence: databasise/evidence/CROSS-MODALITY-EVIDENCE.md:140-148, 197-212, 253 ('MODAL-05 is **discharged**'). `ls v1/.parity_v2_store/shared-4fab18fef508b7bc3dda1cc2d8f12e36` lists hipporag-chunks, hipporag-entities, hipporag-facts, hipporag-graph and hipporag-text-chunks.
gui_impact: None at runtime. Do not use these docstrings to decide whether HippoRAG data exists.

description: The rendered PARITY-EVIDENCE.md cites the dead path three times, from parity_report.py:807, 994 and 1209, all through _GATE_AMENDMENT_REF at line 60. DECLARED-DEVIATIONS.md does not cite it. FALSIFIER-5-EVIDENCE.md also contains the same dead path. The file now lives at .planning/milestones/v1.0-phases/03-lightrag-query-side/03-GATE-AMENDMENT.md.
evidence: `ls .planning/phases/03-lightrag-query-side/03-GATE-AMENDMENT.md` gives 'No such file'. The milestones path exists.
gui_impact: A console that links rendered evidence documents would show a dead link.

description: The package docstring says 'five intention-level tools', and the create_server docstring says 'registers the five tools'. Nine tools are registered.
evidence: tools.py:73-83 TOOL_NAMES has 9 entries. A live list_tools() returned ['ingest','query','compare','delete','status','resolve','promote','rollback','retire'].
gui_impact: None. Use TOOL_NAMES as the source of truth.

description: Packaging is incomplete for a non-editable install. 'databasise.tools' is missing from [tool.setuptools] packages. package-data does not ship evidence/eval-bundles/** (read by eval.remint and eval.aa_run) or tests/fixtures/** (read by corpus_ingest CORPUS_DIR and parity.corpus). The CLIs work today only because databasise/.venv uses an editable finder (__editable___databasise_0_1_0_finder.py).
evidence: The packages list has no 'databasise.tools' although databasise/tools/__init__.py exists. package-data lists only 'databasise.evidence' = ['wirings/*.json'] and 'databasise.wirings'. Importing databasise.tools.check_import_boundary from /tmp works through the editable finder.
gui_impact: A console that shells out to these CLIs must run them from the source checkout (cd databasise && uv run python -m ...), not from a built wheel.

description: The v1 corpus driver implements the ops 'entities' (the entity map for a doc_id) and 'entity_info' (entity details by name). No production code calls them. Only tests/fixtures/v1_corpus_driver_stub.py and real-run tests use them.
evidence: A grep for '"entities"' and '"entity_info"' outside the driver finds only tests/fixtures/v1_corpus_driver_stub.py:68-108. The engine reaches only ingest, delete, status and health.
gui_impact: A LightRAG per-document entity view for the console could reuse these existing ops through a new engine method instead of new v1 code.

description: Neither CLI has an estimate-only default or a --spend gate. build_hipporag_index.main runs a full live OpenIE index build immediately. remint.main always makes one live judge chat call. It mints a new bundle version under evidence/eval-bundles only when the content hash changes (a new judge identity, prompt hash, settings or snapshot). Otherwise mint_bundle returns the existing version.
evidence: remint.py:118-129 runs parser.parse_args(argv) with no arguments, then calls _build_clients and resolve_judge_identity. build_hipporag_index.py:334-338 calls asyncio.run(build_index()) directly.
gui_impact: These must never be one-click console buttons. If shown at all, they need an explicit spend confirmation in the console itself.

description: A trace_token from a partial (degraded) run makes /promote, /rollback and /retire return an unstructured 500 (AssertionError) instead of a named 422 refusal. When the scheduler halts, it appends NodeTraces only for completed and failed nodes. Cancelled siblings and nodes in later batches get no trace entry, so the dispatched node-id set is a strict subset of the wiring's node set and _arm_name_for_node_ids matches no candidate.
evidence: scheduler.py:586-625 appends a NodeTrace for failed nodes only, skips cancelled tasks ('continue' at 618-624) and breaks at 671-677. promotion.py:121-128 requires an exact frozenset equality and otherwise raises AssertionError. Reproduction: Databasise(store_root=tmp, workspace='ws') with clients=None; query(QueryObject(text='hello')) -> partial=True, stop_reason "node 'embedder-query': NodeExecutionError: ... no client is wired under that key", traced nodes ['embedder-index','embedder-query']; then promote('a',[token],'human_edit') raised AssertionError "trace record's own dispatched node id set ['embedder-index', 'embedder-query'] does not match any currently registered wiring's own resolved node id set". rollback and retire run the same precondition before reading the ledger (engine.py:1323-1325, 1464-1466), so they fail the same way even though they discard the arm name.
gui_impact: 'Promote from this result' and the trace pickers for all three ledger forms must exclude tokens whose envelope (or non-debug /trace/resolve) has partial=true. Otherwise the operator gets a bare 500. With an app built without clients, every query trace is partial, so no ledger operation can succeed.

description: The vector half of /health cannot fail. The probe only constructs MultiNamespaceVectorStore, and that constructor assigns three attributes and touches no file or index, so stores.vector is always true.
evidence: vector.py:489-492: __init__ only calls super().__init__(namespace='<multi>') and sets self._store_root and self._children={}. FaissVectorStore children are created only on select(). health() never calls select(), so finalize() iterates an empty dict (vector.py:530-532).
gui_impact: The 'vector' row in the Health panel always shows OK and says nothing about the Faiss indexes. The GUI should label it as not probed, or omit it.

description: storages_initialized carries no information beyond 'subprocess exited 0'. working_dir_present is forced false on any subprocess failure. On success it reports whether v1/.corpus_working_dir existed before this probe's LightRAG constructor ran, so it can be false on a successful first probe and turn overall status to degraded.
evidence: driver 323-326: rag = await _build_rag(...); try: storages_initialized = True. engine.py:954-956 sets both to False in the except branch.
gui_impact: Do not show storages_initialized as a separate diagnostic. Present the pair as one 'v1 engine reachable' indicator. working_dir_present=false does not mean the directory is missing.

description: GET /health is not read-only. On a fresh store root it creates <store_root>/<workspace>/text_chunks/kv.sqlite3 (with a table) and the Cozo RocksDB database <store_root>/<workspace>/chunk_entity_relation/graph.cozo (with the nodes and edges relations). It does this even for a workspace used only by HippoRAG. The v1 health op also creates v1/.corpus_working_dir. The HealthReport docstring presents the operation as a probe.
evidence: SqliteKVStore.__init__ runs mkdir(parents=True), sqlite3.connect and CREATE TABLE (kv.py:51-60). CozoGraphStore.__init__ runs mkdir, CozoClient('rocksdb', ...) and _ensure_relations (graph.py:104-108). Both are called unconditionally in health() (engine.py:938-941). The in-process probe listed text_chunks/kv.sqlite3 and chunk_entity_relation/graph.cozo/data under the temp store root.
gui_impact: Polling /health against a store root the operator has not yet used creates store directories as a side effect. Each probe also takes the RocksDB lock, so health polls can make a concurrent query or ingest fail its own graph open. Section 1 describes only the opposite direction of this contention.

description: The v1 status ops require the eight keys at facade construction. They can come from the server process environment, v1/.env.parity (overlay, adapter 124) or v1/.env (loaded by v1 itself from cwd=v1). If all three lack a key, /corpus and /corpus/counts return an unstructured 500 and /health reports degraded with no reason.
evidence: _build_rag reads os.environ['EMBEDDING_DIM'], ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'], ['EMBEDDING_BINDING_HOST'], ['EMBEDDING_BINDING_API_KEY'] and ['LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE'|'GRAPH'|'VECTOR'|'DOC_STATUS'] at construction (driver 153-166). The adapter loads them only from DEFAULT_V1_ENV_PARITY and returns {} when the file is absent (adapter 86-87, 124).
gui_impact: The launcher and setup documentation must ensure v1/.env.parity exists. The GUI error state for a /corpus 500 should name the v1 configuration as a likely cause.

description: The gate verbs (promote-next, promote-now) can never return UncalibratedFloorRefusalError on a first promotion or across modalities. derive_mutation_class classes any differing node in _INDEX_RECIPE_NODE_IDS as index-side, and every query wiring contains such a node: naive, hybrid, local and global contain 'embedder-index', and hipporag contains chunk-embed, openie and others. A first promotion (prior None, so every node differs) is therefore index-side for every arm except bypass, which is answer-level. The result is MeasurementPostureRefusalError. retrieval-side arises only for a re-promote of the same arm or a hybrid/local/global swap.
evidence: Node sets printed from all_wirings(): naive ['assemble','chunk-vector','embedder-index','embedder-query','generate','heading-backfill','rerank']; hybrid/local/global all include 'embedder-index' and 'keywords'; bypass ['generate']; hipporag includes 'chunk-embed','openie','fact-edges',... promotion.py:220-229.
gui_impact: A gated-verb UI preview would always show the posture refusal for a new alias. This is only a display matter while the gate verbs remain hidden or disabled.

description: The gate-verb posture refusal is raised inside ledger.transaction(), after Ledger(self.store_root) has been constructed. A refused promote-next or promote-now on a fresh store root therefore still creates ledger.db with its schema, indexes and triggers. The same applies to UnknownGenerationVersionError on rollback and retire. The refusal writes no row, but the file is created.
evidence: engine.py:1201 Ledger(...) runs before 1213-1214 enforce_gate_verb_posture. Ledger.__init__ mkdir + connect + _create_schema (ledger.py:138-143).
gui_impact: None functionally. A refused ledger action is not a filesystem no-op.

description: Default-selector (LightRAG) ingest writes into v1's own fixed working directory <repo>/v1/.corpus_working_dir through the v1 subprocess. Every LightRAG query arm reads the machine's own stores at store_root/workspace (SqliteKVStore/MultiNamespaceVectorStore/CozoGraphStore). The only bridge between the two is the one-time parity importer, which reads a different directory (v1/.parity_working_dir) and is not called by any route. A document ingested through POST /documents or /documents/upload with no selector is therefore never visible to POST /query or /compare against LightRAG arms.
evidence: full_ingest.py:219-224 calls run_corpus_op('ingest', payload, timeout=...) with no working_dir, so v1_corpus_adapter.py:129 uses DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = v1/.corpus_working_dir (line 31). engine._execute builds stores via _build_stores(self.store_root, self.workspace, resolved) at engine.py:987. import_index.py:84 DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = v1/.parity_working_dir, and import_v1_index (231) is a parity tool, not called by the seam.
gui_impact: An operator who ingests a document and then queries it gets no evidence from it. The Documents screen (GET /corpus) shows the document as processed while Query shows nothing. The GUI must warn that LightRAG ingest and LightRAG query use disconnected stores, or the engine must be fixed first.

description: A failed node sets stop_reason (and degradation_reason, which is the same value) to f"node {node_id!r}: {cause}". That string reaches the §18.2 ResponseEnvelope unredacted, and also the non-debug /trace/resolve output, because stop_reason and degradation_reason are in _NON_DEBUG_TRACE_FIELDS. §18.2 forbids a consumer receiving a node id. The redact gate does not catch it because assert_no_forbidden_values checks only exact equality, not substring containment (redact.py:20-30).
evidence: Live probe: POST /query {"query":{"text":"x"}} on create_app(store_root=tmp, workspace='ws') with no clients returned 200 with "stop_reason":"node 'embedder-query': NodeExecutionError: declared effect 'calls_embedding' requires client 'embedding', but no client is wired under that key for this run".
gui_impact: The GUI will display internal node ids in the stop-reason banner. The GUI should treat stop_reason as opaque free text and not depend on it for logic. The leak itself needs an engine fix.

description: _node_result_or_refuse inspects only the provides node, graph-augment-persist. When an earlier HippoRAG ingest node such as chunk-embed fails (for example ClientNotWiredError for 'embedding'), the scheduler records the exception under chunk-embed and stops scheduling. The provides node then has neither an exception nor a result, so the refusal carries a synthesized RuntimeError('the \'ingest\' node produced no result and no exception') and the real cause is lost. Section 1's sentence "HippoRAG ingest fails the same way and surfaces as ForeignEngineRefusalError" is true, but the refusal's cause/message does not name the missing client, and the refusal is labelled 'foreign engine' although HippoRAG runs in-process.
evidence: engine.py:385 reads scheduled['node_exceptions'].get(node_id) where node_id = resolved['provides'][0] (engine.py:688). scheduler.py:599 stores the exception under the failing node id, and scheduler.py:671-677 breaks after the failed batch.
gui_impact: A HippoRAG ingest refusal banner will show an unhelpful 'produced no result and no exception' message. The GUI cannot tell the operator that a client is missing.

description: A HippoRAG-selected ingest returns IngestJob(job_id=<engine-minted uuid track_id>). GET /jobs/{job_id} always asks v1's doc-status store (aget_docs_by_track_id), which never saw that track id. total==0 then raises UnknownJobError. HippoRAG ingest jobs can never be polled.
evidence: engine.py:769 job_id=str(result.get('track_id') or track_id), and HippoRAG's graph-augment-persist does not return a v1 track_id. engine.py:862-870 always routes to run_corpus_op('status', {'track_id': job_id,...}) and raises UnknownJobError on total 0.
gui_impact: The Jobs screen will show 'unknown job' (422 UnknownJobError) for every HippoRAG ingest. The GUI must know which modality an ingest went to and skip polling for HippoRAG. Because ingest blocks, HippoRAG's IngestJob response is already final.

description: GET /health has three real problems and one redundant field. (a) It constructs the stores, which creates directories and database files, so an empty or wrong store_root reports all stores true and status 'ok'. (b) It probes only the LightRAG namespaces (text_chunks, chunk_entity_relation), not hipporag-text-chunks or hipporag-graph. (c) storages_initialized duplicates 'the subprocess succeeded': it is set only after initialize_storages() returns, so it carries no information beyond working_dir_present's success path. (d) Any subprocess failure sets working_dir_present to False even when the directory exists (engine.py:954-956).
evidence: Live probe on a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp() store_root: GET /health returned {"status":"ok","stores":{"kv":true,"vector":true,"graph":true},...}.
gui_impact: The health tile can show green for an empty or misconfigured store_root and for HippoRAG stores it never checked. The GUI should label it 'stores openable / v1 reachable', not 'healthy'.

description: Every query, ingest, delete, evidence resolve and health probe opens the embedded-RocksDB CozoGraphStore for one graph namespace directory and holds it for the whole call. A second open of the same directory in the same process fails. Concurrent requests on the same namespace therefore collide: LightRAG /query, /compare, LightRAG ingest (held for up to 900 s), LightRAG delete (up to 300 s), /evidence/resolve and /health all share chunk_entity_relation, while HippoRAG query and ingest share hipporag-graph. A colliding /query, /compare, /evidence/resolve, /documents or DELETE returns 500. A colliding /health returns 200 with graph:false. HippoRAG and LightRAG operations do not collide with each other, except that /health and /evidence/resolve always open chunk_entity_relation.
evidence: Probe: pycozo Client('rocksdb', p) opened twice in one process raised "RocksDB error: IO error: lock hold by current process". Ingest opens stores at engine.py:730 before run_wiring (732) and finalizes only at 752-754.
gui_impact: The GUI must serialize all engine calls except /trace/resolve and the ledger routes, and must disable Query while an ingest is running.

description: A caller-supplied document_id failing the token regex raises a bare ValueError from generated_on_disk_name on ingest, which becomes an unhandled 500. On DELETE the same check is mapped to UnknownDocumentError (engine.py:800-803). The two write paths map the same input error differently.
evidence: Live probe: POST /documents {"document":{"text":"hi","document_id":"../bad"}} returned 500 text/plain 'Internal Server Error'.
gui_impact: The GUI should validate document_id client-side against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ before submitting ingest.

description: Inside FastAPI JSON body validation, only AmbiguousIngestPayloadError embeds its class name in detail[].msg. ForbiddenSelectorInputError and OversizedDocumentError do not, and the selector at-most-one rule is a plain ValueError with ctx.error {}. The GUI must identify them by ctx.error key set: {set_members} means ambiguous payload, {actual_bytes, limit_bytes} means oversized, {member_name, value} means forbidden selector value, and {} with 'at most one of' in msg means a multi-member selector. PageSizeExceededError is a normal refusal 422 with refusal_type on REST. On /documents/upload, ambiguous or oversized payloads are 500, and selector errors are MalformedSelectorPayloadError 422.
evidence: Live probes: the selector with alias+capability gave ctx.error {}; the hash-shaped alias gave msg "Value error, selector member 'alias' carries a value shaped like an internal identity: ..." with ctx.error {member_name, value}; the empty document gave msg "Value error, AmbiguousIngestPayloadError: ..." with ctx.error {set_members: []}.
gui_impact: The GUI must identify these by ctx.error key set: {set_members} means ambiguous payload, {actual_bytes, limit_bytes} means oversized, {member_name, value} means forbidden selector input, {} plus the 'at most one of' message text means selector multi-member. Class-name matching only works for one of them.

description: ForeignEngineRefusalError.cause is stringified into the 422 body. For a v1 subprocess failure that string contains up to 2000 characters of the v1 Python traceback (stderr), including absolute server file paths and missing env-var names.
evidence: _refusal_response sets value = str(value) for BaseException attributes (rest.py:229-230). CorpusOpSubprocessError message = f"v1 corpus driver subprocess exited {returncode}: {stderr.strip()[:2000]}" (v1_corpus_adapter.py:64).

description: IngestDocument's validator raises AmbiguousIngestPayloadError or OversizedDocumentError inside the tool body. Pydantic wraps it in a ValidationError, which is not a SeamRefusalError, so _refusal_mapped does not catch it. The SDK then turns it into UnexpectedToolError, which by design withholds the original text. The MCP client gets no refusal_type and no reason. The tools.py module docstring (lines 6-9) says MCP defers to IngestDocument as 'the single source of truth' for the same validation REST uses. REST returns a 422 validation body that does carry the reason.
evidence: Probe: ingest {} gave exc=UnexpectedToolError, msg='Error executing tool ingest'. Its cause was 'ValidationError: ... AmbiguousIngestPayloadError: ... got [] set'. Over the wire (mcp.Client) the result was is_error=true, text='Error executing tool ingest'. Ingest with both text and raw gave the same, with cause got ['text','raw']. Ingest with text of 25 MiB + 1 byte gave UnexpectedToolError, cause 'ingest document is 26214401 bytes, exceeding the 26214400-byte cap'. REST POST /documents with {document:{}} returned 422 {detail:[{msg:'Value error, AmbiguousIngestPayloadError: ...', ctx:{error:{set_members:[]}}}]}. The SDK behaviour is in .venv/.../mcp/server/mcpserver/tools/base.py:205-210 (a generic Exception becomes UnexpectedToolError(f'Error executing tool {name}')) and exceptions.py:61-71 ('nothing from the original reaches the client'). The SDK also logs it at ERROR with a traceback (server.py:450-451).
gui_impact: GUI uses REST, so there is no direct impact. Any MCP client, including an agent-driven console, gets no reason for a rejected ingest. If MCP is ever offered to an operator, the fix is to catch pydantic.ValidationError in ingest_tool and re-raise the inner SeamRefusalError, which is available as exc.errors()[0]['ctx']['error'].

description: Raw-bytes ingest (POST /documents/upload, or POST /documents with `raw`) on the LightRAG path never parses the uploaded file. The engine stamps documents=[{id, text:""}], file_paths=[inbox path] and docs_format=pending_parse. The driver always passes `ids=` to apipeline_enqueue_documents. v1 gives explicit ids priority over docs_format and always enqueues the sanitized `input` text as RAW, so it enqueues an empty-content RAW document and never reads the bytes written to corpus-inbox.
evidence: engine.py:711 `node_config["documents"] = [{"id": document_id, "document_id": document_id, "text": ""}]`, :713 docs_format=pending_parse; driver :180-191 always passes `ids=ids`; v1 pipeline.py:561-571: "`ids` outranks `docs_format` by design ... always enqueues the sanitized body as RAW" followed by `if ids is not None: ... _add_content(i, cleaned_content, FULL_DOCS_FORMAT_RAW)`. The tests mock the driver and only assert that config docs_format == 'pending_parse' (tests/parts_core/lightrag/test_full_ingest.py:285-303), so no test runs the real v1 path.
gui_impact: The Upload-file tab reports success with job_id and enqueued=1, but the document's content is never indexed. The GUI must not present upload as working for LightRAG until this is fixed.

description: Because of D1, every LightRAG raw upload has content "" and therefore the same content hash. From the second upload on (with any new document_id), v1's content-hash dedup rejects the upload: it writes a FAILED `dup-...` doc-status record ('Identical content already exists under another filename.') under the caller's track_id and enqueues nothing. A text ingest with `text: ""` (accepted by IngestDocument, corpus.py:79-81) collides the same way.
evidence: pipeline.py:510-512 content_hash = compute_text_content_hash(content or "") for RAW; :683-700 hash match marks the document a duplicate; :758-781 creates a FAILED record with track_id=current track_id and error_msg 'Identical content already exists...'.
gui_impact: GET /jobs/{job_id} for the second and later uploads shows one failed row whose document_id is `dup-<hash>`, not the caller's id. The GUI should expect and explain these rows.

description: IngestJob.enqueued reports the number of documents submitted, not the number v1 actually enqueued. When v1 drops the document as a duplicate (same document_id already present via filter_keys, same basename, or same content hash), apipeline_enqueue_documents returns None with nothing enqueued. The driver still returns enqueued=len(documents)=1, and the route returns 200.
evidence: driver:198 `return {"track_id": result_track_id, "enqueued": len(documents), "usage": None}`; pipeline.py:648 filter_keys, :797-800 `if not new_docs: logger.warning("No new unique documents were found."); return`; engine.py:769 falls back to the engine track_id when result track_id is None.
gui_impact: enqueued cannot be trusted as success. The GUI must poll /jobs and read the row status. Re-ingesting an existing document_id is a no-op plus a failed dup record, not an update: the operator must DELETE first.

description: A failed HippoRAG ingest leaves a partial write committed. run_wiring records node failures instead of raising. ingest() then calls index_done_callback() on every store, which commits pending writes, and only afterwards calls _node_result_or_refuse, which raises ForeignEngineRefusalError. If chunk-embed succeeds and a later node fails (for example openie with no llm client, or an LLM error), the hipporag-chunks vectors and hipporag-text-chunks KV records are committed while the caller receives 422.
evidence: engine.py:750-751 `for store in stores.values(): await store.index_done_callback()` runs inside the try before :761 `result = _node_result_or_refuse(scheduled, result_node_id, "ingest")`; chunk_embed.py:96-119 stages vector and kv upserts; scheduler.py:586-620 records the failure and stops later batches without raising.
gui_impact: After a 422 ForeignEngineRefusalError on a HippoRAG ingest, the document's chunks can still appear in HippoRAG query evidence. HippoRAG has no delete path to remove them.

description: The LightRAG write path and read path use different stores, and no shipped command connects them. Ingest and delete run v1 against v1/.corpus_working_dir. The LightRAG query arms read the v2 stores under <store_root>/<workspace>/ (`chunks` vector, `text_chunks` kv). The only writer of those v2 stores is parity/import_index.py. Its CLI imports from v1/.parity_working_dir into DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT and a corpus-hash-derived workspace, with no argument to change any of them.
evidence: v1_corpus_adapter.py:31 DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = v1/.corpus_working_dir; import_index.py:84 DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR = v1/.parity_working_dir; import_index.py:506-509 main() hard-codes DEFAULT_V1_WORKING_DIR and DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT; parts_core/lightrag/chunk_vector.py:28 reads ctx.stores["vector"].select("chunks").
gui_impact: A document ingested through POST /documents never becomes queryable or resolvable through /query or /evidence/resolve on a LightRAG selector, and DELETE /documents/{id} does not remove it from query results. Only /corpus and /jobs reflect LightRAG writes. The console must label this or keep LightRAG ingest and delete separate from LightRAG query.

description: Section 3.3 lists no 500 for graph-store lock contention, but ingest, delete and evidence resolution each open an embedded RocksDB CozoGraphStore before their try block. A LightRAG ingest holds `chunk_entity_relation` for the whole v1 subprocess run, up to 900 s. A concurrent LightRAG query, delete, evidence resolve or second LightRAG ingest in the same process fails while constructing the store and returns an unstructured 500. Concurrent HippoRAG ingest and HippoRAG query contend on `hipporag-graph` the same way.
evidence: engine.py:730 `stores = _build_stores(...)` precedes `try:` at :731; :822 likewise precedes :823; graph.py:106 `self._client = CozoClient("rocksdb", str(self._db_path))` in __init__; hipporag corpus-ingest.json store_namespaces graph = hipporag-graph.
gui_impact: The GUI must serialize writes against queries and evidence resolution, for example by disabling Query and Delete while an ingest is in flight, and must map 500s that occur during an ingest to a 'store busy' message.

description: A trace from a partial run cannot be used for promote, rollback or retire. Cancelled siblings and later batches are absent. _arm_name_for_node_ids requires an exact match with a candidate wiring's full node set and raises AssertionError when nothing matches, so the route returns an unstructured 500 instead of a refusal.

description: Every /evidence/resolve call constructs a new FaissVectorStore for the namespace. Construction reads the whole index file, SHA-256 hashes it and loads the full sidecar JSON. The call also opens and creates a SQLite text_chunks database and a RocksDB chunk_entity_relation graph under the workspace, even though only the vector store is read.
evidence: vector.py:126-137 checksum and read_index in __init__; engine.py:1089 `_build_stores(self.store_root, self.workspace)`; kv.py:51-54 and graph.py:104-107 mkdir and open.
gui_impact: Per-reference latency grows with index size. Resolving N evidence rows costs N full index loads, so client-side caching and lazy resolution are necessary, not optional.

description: HippoRAG chunk ids are sha256(f"{document_id}:{ordinal}"), so re-ingesting the same document_id with different text overwrites the metadata behind an existing EvidenceRef. Chunks beyond the new chunk count keep their old text. An old evidence ref then resolves to content that differs from what the earlier answer used, without any error.

description: Refusals raised inside pydantic validators during JSON body parsing (ForbiddenSelectorInputError, the selector one-member ValueError, AmbiguousIngestPayloadError, OversizedDocumentError) return HTTP 422 as documented, but in FastAPI's {detail:[...]} validation shape with no refusal_type. description: _refusal_mapped catches only SeamRefusalError, so validator-wrapped refusals and Page ValueErrors that occur inside tool bodies surface as the SDK's UnexpectedToolError with no refusal_type. Untested cases: an ingest with both or neither of text/raw_base64, an oversized payload, and status with a negative offset.
evidence: Reproduced: call_tool('status', {args:{scope:'corpus', offset:-1}}) -> UnexpectedToolError 'Error executing tool status'; call_tool('ingest', {args:{text:'x', raw_base64:'eA=='}}) -> UnexpectedToolError; call_tool('ingest', {args:{}}) -> UnexpectedToolError. StatusToolArgs.offset has no ge=0 (tools.py:161).
gui_impact: Not GUI-facing. It is a REST/MCP parity gap.

description: After a rollback to version V, retire(V) succeeds. The alias still resolves to V's wiring, which is the exact outcome retire()'s docstring says the active-generation guard prevents (engine.py:1430-1437). The guard compares only active.minted_version == version. A rollback row mints a new version (W) and records V only in targets_version, so V passes the guard. Every retire test seeds promote(naive), promote(bypass), retire(1.0.0) and never retires a version that a rollback targets.
evidence: Reproduced: promote naive -> 1.0.0, promote bypass -> 2.0.0, rollback to 1.0.0 -> 3.0.0, then retire 1.0.0 returns record_kind='tombstone'. Afterwards Ledger.by_alias = rollback row with mutation_id 'naive', targets_version '1.0.0', and _resolve_alias(alias) == resolve_arm('naive'). The API-INVENTORY notes this only as an 'Edge' (line 563).
gui_impact: After a rollback the console can show an alias serving a wiring whose generation is tombstoned. The retire picker should block a version that the active rollback row targets.

description: Same defect. The test reference is test_operator_verb_concurrency.py:41 (_SIX_ARMS includes 'hipporag') and 121-148 (test_six_concurrent_promotes_mint_six_distinct_versions_with_zero_exceptions). That test promotes all six arms, including hipporag, to one alias and never resolves the alias.
evidence: Reproduced: promote('hp', [hipporag trace]) -> version 1.0.0; _resolve_alias('hp') -> UnknownArmError "unknown arm 'hipporag'; known arms: ['bypass','global','hybrid','local','naive']". UnknownArmError(ValueError) at wirings/resolve.py:38. No test calls query with an alias whose mutation_id is hipporag.
gui_impact: A HippoRAG promotion done from the console breaks every later /query, /query/stream or /compare that uses that alias (500, and the message lists arm names).

description: A HippoRAG ingest returns a job_id that cannot be polled. The job_id is an engine-minted uuid track_id, but get_job_status, corpus_status and document_counts only query the v1 LightRAG driver, so polling a HippoRAG job raises UnknownJobError and HippoRAG documents never appear in /corpus. The HippoRAG ingest tests assert that job_id is truthy and never poll it.
evidence: engine.py:769 returns IngestJob(job_id=result.get('track_id') or track_id); engine.py:862-870 calls run_corpus_op('status', {track_id}) and raises UnknownJobError when total == 0. No test polls /jobs for a HippoRAG job.
gui_impact: The jobs drawer must not offer polling for HippoRAG ingests, and the corpus browser shows LightRAG documents only.

description: After a real HippoRAG ingest, evidence refs from the PPR path do not resolve. PPR emits item ids with a 'chunk:' prefix, while chunk-embed writes vector and KV records under the bare sha256 chunk_id. The write-path test avoids this on purpose: its stub fact-filter always returns keep_ids=[] so that dpr-fallback is used instead of ppr.
evidence: ppr.py:85 emits {'id': name} only for names that start with 'chunk:'; chunk_embed.py:98 and 118 upsert ids=[record['chunk_id']] with no prefix. The test docstring at test_hipporag_write_path.py:62-69 states that content hydration and evidence resolution 'would look up a key neither store holds'.
gui_impact: On HippoRAG answers whose facts survive filtering, 'Open evidence' returns UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError.

description: DuplicateComparisonKeyError is only checked inside the per-arm loop. Arms before the duplicate have already run, which means LLM/embedding spend and trace records persisted to trace.db, and then the whole result is discarded. No behavioural test covers the duplicate refusal; it appears only as a synthetic factory entry.
evidence: compare_arms awaits execute() for each selector before testing `if key in results` on the next one. engine.compare (engine.py:644-650) pre-resolves selectors but does not pre-check keys. grep finds DuplicateComparisonKeyError only in the test_rest_transport.py import and factory list.
gui_impact: The compare screen should de-duplicate selector keys on the client before submitting.

description: MutableStoreComparisonExcludedError is unreachable in production. Tests reach it only through the cbm_reachable fixture, which monkeypatches selectors._capability_candidates (test_mutable_store_exclusion.py:62-76; the module docstring at line 8 states that the wiring is not resolvable through production selectors). Separately, the one-selector compare path (engine.py:642-643) never runs this check.
evidence: The test module docstring states that the codebase-memory-mcp wiring 'is not resolvable through any of §18.4's four production selectors today'. The cbm_reachable fixture patches the candidate pool.
gui_impact: The compare screen can leave out the mutates_store exclusion state for now.

description: The test does not check what its docstring claims. The docstring says it proves that a malicious upload filename never reaches the on-disk name. The test only asserts generated_on_disk_name(response.json()['job_id'] or 'deadbeef'), and job_id is the track_id, not the document_id or the file written under corpus-inbox/. Even a file written under the caller's filename would pass.
evidence: There is no assertion on store_root/corpus-inbox contents. The `or "deadbeef"` fallback means the assertion passes even when job_id is empty.
gui_impact: none directly. Upload path safety is not actually covered by a test.

description: The round-trip tests never check counts after delete. The REST test checks only status 200 for the second /corpus/counts, and the in-process test asserts second_counts.total >= 0, which is always true.
evidence: Line 442: `assert second_counts_response.status_code == 200` and nothing else. Line 481: `assert second_counts.total >= 0`.
gui_impact: Nothing proves that counts change after a delete, so the console should re-poll and not compute counts itself.

description: limit has no lower bound. limit=0 and negative limits are accepted on GET /corpus, GET /jobs and the MCP status tool, and are passed to the v1 driver. A negative REST offset returns FastAPI's validation 422, not PageSizeExceeded-style refusal shape. None of this is tested; only the upper cap is.
evidence: Reproduced: GET /corpus?limit=-5 -> 200, GET /corpus?limit=0 -> 200, GET /corpus?offset=-1 -> 422 {detail:[{type:'greater_than_equal'...}]}. Page._bounded checks only limit > MAX_PAGE_SIZE and offset < 0.
gui_impact: The pager must clamp limit to 1..100 on the client.

description: The leak tests treat part name@version as forbidden, while SeamEvent.component exposes it on ResponseEnvelope and DeletionOutcome. The contract does not forbid names (CONTRACT.md:114). The closer contract gap is that §14 item 4 (CONTRACT.md:630) asks the seam event to record the resolved capability, and the code records name@version instead. Classify this as a test/contract inconsistency, not a confirmed violation.
evidence: test_mach11_event.py:375 asserts event.component == LIGHTRAG_FULL_DELETE_PART.name_at_version. test_compare.py:237-238 adds registry.keys() to the forbidden set for envelopes.
gui_impact: The seam-events table on the delete result will show modality-specific part names. The rule (whether they are allowed) is not settled.

description: MCP scope-precondition errors ('scope job requires a job_id', missing evidence_ref or trace_reference) are raised as plain-text ToolErrors with no JSON refusal_type. The tests check only for a ToolError, and the MCP NoWritePath delete test does not check refusal_type either. The resolve tool's 'trace' scope has no test at all.
evidence: grep for '"scope": "trace"' under tests/mcp and tests/seam returns nothing.
gui_impact: none for the REST GUI

description: An alias whose active ledger row has mutation_id 'hipporag' raises UnknownArmError (an unmapped ValueError subclass, so HTTP 500) on every operation that resolves a selector, not only /query, /query/stream and /compare. Ingest, upload and delete under that alias also fail, because ingest() and delete_document() call resolve_selector before _corpus_wiring.
evidence: Reproduced in-process: after appending a ledger row with alias='h', mutation_id='hipporag', engine.query, engine.ingest and engine.delete_document with Selector(alias='h') all raise UnknownArmError("unknown arm 'hipporag'; known arms: ['bypass', 'global', 'hybrid', 'local', 'naive']"). _resolve_alias returns resolve_arm(record.mutation_id) (selectors.py:269), and resolve_arm accepts only _ARM_NAMES (resolve.py:30, 86-89).
gui_impact: Inventory 5.2 row 1 must list /documents, /documents/upload and DELETE /documents/{id} as affected too. The GUI cannot use an alias selector on the Ingest or Delete forms for a HippoRAG alias without getting a 500 that names the internal arms.

description: Promote, rollback and retire return HTTP 500 (AssertionError) for any trace produced by a partial run. The scheduler records only the nodes it dispatched, and _arm_name_for_node_ids requires the dispatched node-id set to equal a wiring's full node set. Any run halted by a node failure or a budget halt therefore cannot be used as promotion evidence, and the caller gets a 500 instead of a named refusal. Rollback and retire are affected too, because they share _resolve_operator_preconditions.
evidence: Reproduced: with clients=None, engine.query(QueryObject(text='x')) gives partial=True and the debug trace lists only ['embedder-index','embedder-query']. engine.promote('n',[token],'human_edit') then raises AssertionError("trace record's own dispatched node id set ['embedder-index', 'embedder-query'] does not match any currently registered wiring's own resolved node id set"). The same happens for a HippoRAG run (dispatched ['chunk-embed','fact-score']). Over REST: POST /promote returns 500.
gui_impact: 'Promote from this result' must be disabled for partial results. The inventory's promote helper (3.2.2: 'compare the sets of nodes[].node_id') also fails, because a partial trace's node set is a subset of the wiring's. Missing from 5.2.

description: The hybrid and global LightRAG arms cannot be reached through any selector. Under capability matching, local has the same effect union as hybrid with fewer nodes (15 vs 17), and the same effect union and node count as global; the stable sort keeps local first. The default always resolves to naive and harness always refuses. An alias needs a promote from a trace that ran the arm, and no seam path produces such a trace. Only naive, bypass, local and hipporag are reachable.
evidence: Computed with default_registry(): the effect unions of hybrid, local and global are all {calls_embedding, calls_llm, calls_rerank, reads_graph, reads_kv, reads_vector, writes_artifact}; node counts are naive 7, bypass 1, hybrid 17, local 15, global 15, hipporag 13. _match_capability sorts by len(nodes) with a stable sort (selectors.py:163), so local always wins over hybrid and global.
gui_impact: The Compare screen cannot put hybrid or global side by side with the other arms. A proposed GET /wirings row should mark them unreachable, or selection needs a tie-break that is not based on node count. Missing from the inventory.

description: Graph-store lock contention is broader than inventory 5.2 states. Any two overlapping calls in one process that open the same Cozo namespace collide: two /query calls, /compare, /query/stream, LightRAG ingest or delete, evidence resolve and health. _build_stores constructs kv, then vector, then graph in one dict literal outside the try/finally, so when the graph open raises, the already-open kv and vector stores are never finalized.
evidence: Reproduced: holding CozoGraphStore('chunk_entity_relation','w',root) open, a second open raises 'RocksDB error: IO error: lock hold by current process'. engine.query(QueryObject(text='x')) and engine.resolve_evidence(...) both raise; engine.health() returns stores.graph=False. The stores are built in a dict literal at engine.py:342-346, before the try at 731/823/988/1090.
gui_impact: The GUI must serialize every query, compare, ingest, delete and evidence call per graph namespace, not only health and evidence probes. 5.2 row 6 understates the scope.

description: MCP ingest with raw_base64 containing no valid base64 characters, and REST upload of a 0-byte file, are both accepted with no validation. The seam returns a successful IngestJob and writes a 0-byte file to corpus-inbox. Whether v1 then indexes an empty document or marks it failed is decided downstream; the reproduction showed failed.
evidence: Reproduced: server.call_tool('ingest', {'args': {'raw_base64': '!!!!'}}) returned {job_id, enqueued: 1}. A 0-byte file was written to <store_root>/corpus-inbox, and v1 recorded document 'dup-15f6f452b1ea8f4a9c36928aa0d86588' as failed ('Identical content already exists under another filename').
gui_impact: The inventory's section 4 note ('non-alphabet characters are dropped silently') understates this: a fully invalid string becomes a successful empty ingest. The GUI upload must refuse 0-byte files client-side.

description: Confirmed: an oversized upload, and a caller document_id that fails ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ on either ingest route, return a plain 500 with no body.
evidence: TestClient: an upload of 25 MiB + 1 byte returns 500 'Internal Server Error'; an upload with document_id '../x' returns 500; POST /documents with document_id '../x' returns 500. engine.delete_document already maps the same check to UnknownDocumentError (engine.py:800-803), so the fix can reuse that refusal.
gui_impact: As the inventory states: client-side pre-checks are required.

description: Confirmed: EvidenceRef.namespace is unvalidated, so /evidence/resolve creates directories outside the workspace and outside the store root (both '../..' and absolute paths) before returning 422.
evidence: TestClient: POST /evidence/resolve with namespace '../../evilns' returned 422 UnresolvableEvidenceReferenceError, and the directory <store_root>/../evilns now exists. MultiNamespaceVectorStore.select('<absolute path>') created that absolute directory. _NAMESPACE_TOKEN_RE '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$' (namespaces.py:37) accepts every current vector namespace (chunks, entities, relationships, hipporag-chunks, hipporag-entities, hipporag-facts), so the proposed fix does not break existing namespaces.
gui_impact: As the inventory states.

description: Confirmed: limit has no lower bound. limit=0 makes next_offset equal offset, and a negative limit slices document_ids[offset:offset+limit], which can return more than 100 entries.
evidence: Page._bounded checks only limit > MAX_PAGE_SIZE and offset < 0 (corpus.py:136-139). The driver computes page_ids = document_ids[offset : offset + limit] (driver:300). engine.py:895-900 computes next_offset = offset + len(documents).
gui_impact: As the inventory states.

description: Every Ledger() construction runs no-op DDL and a commit, and Ledger has no close(), so _resolve_alias leaks one sqlite connection per alias-selected call until garbage collection. In WAL mode, on an existing schema, construction does not block on a concurrent promote's BEGIN IMMEDIATE (measured 0.0 s), so read-only ledger routes are feasible over Ledger() as it is. The ledger.py:184-187 docstring that says construction stalls for the busy timeout is wrong.
evidence: ledger.py:143 calls self._create_schema() in __init__; ledger.py:248-251 runs DROP INDEX and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX; transaction() docstring ledger.py:184-187 states the next Ledger() construction stalls for the busy timeout while a write transaction is open.
gui_impact: Feasibility caveat for the proposed ledger listing routes (5.1 rows 'Alias list' and 'Versions and history'): they need a read-only Ledger open path.

description: The MCP docstrings say 'five tools' while nine are registered. The PartRegistry docstring says default_registry holds 'exactly D-04's seven Phase-1 entries'; it holds 35, including 4 fake or fixture parts.
